## 是什么

CELL-FM 是一个虚拟显微镜生成模型：给定蛋白质氨基酸序列和细胞上下文（细胞核、微管、内质网等通道的荧光图像），它生成该蛋白质在细胞中应有的荧光图像；反过来，给定图像，它生成与之兼容的蛋白质序列。它由 BoHuangLab 开发，对应论文 *Virtual experiments bridge sequence and microscopy with generative models*（bioRxiv 2026）。

## 亮点

- **端到端生成而非分类**：直接学习生成实验读数（荧光图像），而不是压缩成定位类别等标签，因此一个模型可服务多种下游问题，无需针对每个任务重训。
- **多模态统一编码器**：图像（VAE patch tokens）和序列（ESM-C 600M 嵌入）在单一 transformer 中联合注意力，融合成共享表示。
- **三头架构**：图像生成（MMDiT + flow matching）、序列生成（离散扩散，order-agnostic autoregressive）、图像重建（masked autoencoder），两阶段训练（先 mask 后全量微调）。
- **表达水平条件化**：CondenSeq 中引入连续表达水平 token，支持同一序列在不同浓度下的虚拟成像，实现 in silico 滴定。
- **大规模真实数据**：HPA（1.1M 单细胞图像）、OpenCell（96K 图像）、CondenSeq（8M 图像，14,598 个无序肽段）。
- **易用性**：提供 Colab 笔记本，一键运行，T4 GPU 即可。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题聚焦 IDR/IDP × 分子互作 × 计算与 AI。CELL-FM 直接针对无序肽段（CondenSeq 数据集）进行虚拟成像，可生成不同表达水平下的凝聚/弥散图像，并输出滴定曲线（AUC、AAC），为研究 IDR 的相分离倾向提供高通量、可解释的预测工具。其方法学可迁移：
- **序列→图像生成**：可用于预测 IDR 在细胞内的空间分布（如核/质定位、凝聚体形成），辅助理解 IDR 介导的互作与相分离。
- **图像→序列生成**：可设计具有特定定位或凝聚特性的 IDR 序列，用于合成生物学或突变设计。
- **表达水平条件化**：为 IDR 的浓度依赖性相分离行为提供建模思路，可迁移到其他 IDR 系统。
- **多模态融合**：将序列语言模型与图像生成结合，为 IDR 的构象系综与细胞表型关联提供新范式。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：仓库根目录为 `cell_fm/`，包含模型、数据集、训练 pipeline 和任务；`scripts/` 提供训练/评估启动脚本；`notebooks/` 提供应用示例。
- **安装与依赖**：README 未列出具体依赖文件（如 requirements.txt），但笔记本会自行安装依赖并下载权重。建议查看 `notebooks/README.md` 获取依赖 pin 信息。
- **输入/输出格式**：输入为蛋白质序列（FASTA 或类似格式）和细胞上下文图像（HPA/OpenCell 格式）；输出为生成的荧光图像（PNG/TIFF 等）或序列（文本）。CondenSeq 应用输出滴定曲线（AUC/AAC）。
- **GPU 需求**：需要 GPU（Colab T4 即可），训练和推理均需 CUDA。
- **调试入口**：`notebooks/condensate_titration.ipynb` 是最直接的示例，可断点调试；`cell_fm/apps/condenseq/` 包含 pipeline 和 metrics 代码。

## 核心 idea

CELL-FM 的核心方法学是**将实验读数本身作为学习目标**，通过生成模型（flow matching + discrete diffusion）在共享多模态表示上实现序列与图像的互转，从而避免任务特定标签的压缩损失，使模型能泛化到多种下游分析。其关键创新在于：
- 用 VAE 将图像压缩为 patch tokens，与 ESM-C 序列嵌入在统一 transformer 中融合，实现跨模态对齐。
- 通过两阶段训练（mask 辅助重建 + 全量生成微调）增强表示鲁棒性。
- 引入表达水平条件 token，使生成过程可控制浓度，支持虚拟滴定实验。

## 可搬移点

- **多模态融合编码器**（`cell_fm/models/cell_fm/modules/transformer.py`）：可解耦用于 IDR 序列与图像特征的联合表示学习，迁移到自定义 pipeline 中。
- **flow matching 图像生成模块**（`cell_fm/models/cell_fm/modules/transport/`）：可复用于生成 IDR 构象系综或相分离图像。
- **离散扩散序列生成器**（`cell_fm/models/cell_fm/modules/`）：可用于设计 IDR 序列，实现反向生成。
- **CondenSeq 滴定 pipeline**（`cell_fm/apps/condenseq/pipeline.py`）：可直接用于 IDR 相分离倾向评估，替换其中的模型或数据即可。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，可放心搬移。

注意：具体模块的接口和依赖需查看源码确认，README 未提供详细 API 文档。
readme:
# CELL-FM

**CELL-FM** is a virtual microscopy model. From a protein's amino-acid sequence and a cellular
context, it generates the fluorescence image that protein would give; from an image, it
generates sequences consistent with it.

Code for [*Virtual experiments bridge sequence and microscopy with generative models*](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.13.751243v1)
(Dihan Zheng, Kibeom Hong, Bo Huang).

| | |
|---|---|
| Paper | [bioRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.09.13.751243](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.13.751243v1) |
| Weights | [huggingface.co/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM](https://huggingface.co/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM) |
| Hugging Face demo | [huggingface.co/spaces/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM](https://huggingface.co/spaces/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM) |

## Virtual experiments

Predictive models usually compress an experiment into task-specific labels, such as a
localization class, before learning. CELL-FM instead learns to generate the experimental
readout itself: the image of a protein in a cell. Phenotypes are then measured on generated
images with the same analysis used on real ones — a nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio, a condensate
classifier, an image embedding. One model serves many downstream questions without retraining,
and its results stay directly comparable to the real assay.

## Method

CELL-FM models images as a continuous distribution and protein sequences as a discrete one,
with a shared encoder and a separate decoder for each output.

**Tokens.** The protein channel and the cell-context channels (the nucleus, plus microtubules and
ER for HPA) are encoded by a VAE and cut into patch tokens. The sequence is embedded with the
ESM-C 600M protein language model.

**Unified encoder.** A single transformer attends over image and sequence tokens together and
fuses them into one shared representation.

**Three heads** read from that representation:

| Head | Objective | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Image generator (MMDiT) | Flow matching in VAE latent space | sequence + cell → protein image |
| Sequence generator | Discrete diffusion (order-agnostic autoregressive) | image + cell → sequence |
| Image reconstruction | Denoising masked autoencoder | auxiliary, stage 1 only |

**Training.** Stage 1 optimizes all three losses with half of the image patches masked, to learn
a robust shared representation. Stage 2 turns masking off and fine-tunes the two generative
losses for fidelity.

**Sampling.** An image is generated by integrating the learned flow from Gaussian noise and
decoding the latent with the VAE. A sequence starts fully masked and is filled in one position
at a time, in random order.

**Expression level.** For CondenSeq, protein expression level is an extra continuous
conditioning token, so the same sequence can be imaged at any concentration. This is what makes
*in silico* titration possible.

### Training data

| Dataset | What it images | Scale | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Human Protein Atlas](https://virtualcellmodels.cziscience.com/dataset/hpa-subcellular-section) | Immunofluorescence in fixed cells; nucleus, microtubule and ER context | 12,894 proteins, 1.1 M single-cell images | Pretraining, localization, signal design |
| [OpenCell](https://opencell.sf.czbiohub.org/) | Endogenously tagged proteins in live HEK293T; nucleus context | 1,311 proteins, ~96,000 single-cell images | Fine-tuning from HPA for virtual staining |
| [CondenSeq](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/bioimages/studies/S-BIAD1738) | Intrinsically disordered peptides in U2OS nuclei, pooled screen; nucleus context | 14,598 peptides of 66 aa, ~8 M single-cell images | Condensate formation across expression levels |

## Applications

Each application is a Colab notebook in [`notebooks/`](notebooks). Choose a GPU runtime (a Colab
T4 works); the notebook installs its own dependencies and downloads the weights on first run.

| Notebook | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [Condensate titration](notebooks/condensate_titration.ipynb) | Images a 66-aa intrinsically disordered peptide along a ladder of expression levels, calls each image condensed or diffuse with a ViT classifier, and turns the calls into a titration curve summarised by **AUC** (propensity to condense) and **AAC** (re-entrant dissolution at high concentration). | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/condensate_titration.ipynb) |
| [NLS screening](notebooks/nls_screening.ipynb) | Slides a window along a protein sequence, virtually stains a cell with each fragment, and scores the nucleus-to-cytoplasm signal ratio per window to locate nuclear localization signals. | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/nls_screening.ipynb) |
| [Localization signal generation](notebooks/pls_generation.ipynb) | Runs the model from image to sequence: shown a cell whose protein sits in the nucleus or in the cytoplasm, it designs NLS or NES peptides, then compares their residue composition with the human proteome. | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/pls_generation.ipynb) |
| [OpenCell virtual staining](notebooks/opencell_vs.ipynb) | Paints any OpenCell protein onto the same nucleus from its sequence, then embeds the generated cells with a ViT to map where proteins localize. | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/opencell_vs.ipynb) |

one_liner: BayesFRET 是一个基于 HDP-HMM 贝叶斯方法分析 smFRET 数据、估计无序蛋白构象状态数及行为的 GUI 工具，直接面向 IDP 构象分析，但聚焦单分子构象状态而非分子互作机制建模。

## 是什么

**BayesFRET** 是一个基于 Python 的 GUI 程序，实现了非参数贝叶斯方法（HDP-HMM，即层次狄利克雷过程-隐马尔可夫模型），用于从表面固定的单分子 FRET（smFRET）实验中估计固有无序蛋白（IDP）等分子的不同构象状态数量及其行为。它支持真实实验数据或合成数据，通过 4 条 MCMC 链进行推断，并输出图表和数值结果。

## 亮点

- **非参数贝叶斯推断**：无需预先指定状态数，自动从数据中学习构象状态数量，适合 IDP 的复杂构象景观。
- **实验信息整合**：将实验参数（如光子发射率、光物理先验）纳入模型，提高推断准确性。
- **GUI 与系统托盘集成**：提供直观的图形界面，支持拖放文件、实时状态显示，并可在 Windows/macOS 上运行。
- **合成数据模式**：可生成模拟数据用于测试和验证，便于方法开发和调试。
- **结果可复现**：保存所有参数、随机种子和采样历史，支持后续分析和可视化。

## 为何对本课题有用

BayesFRET 直接针对 IDP 的构象状态识别问题，是 IDR/IDP 分子互作与构象系综研究的典型工具。其核心方法 HDP-HMM 能够从噪声较大的 smFRET 时间序列中自动推断状态数和状态转移，这对于理解 IDP 的构象动态和相分离（LLPS）中的多态互作至关重要。此外，其合成数据生成模块可用于生成基准数据集，评估其他构象系综采样或预测方法的性能。

## 怎么用

- **入口文件**：`begin.py` 启动 GUI。
- **依赖**：见 `requirements.txt`，包括 `chime`、`darkdetect`、`matplotlib`、`numpy`、`PySide6`、`scipy`。
- **数据格式**：实验模式需要两个文本/CSV 文件，分别包含受体和供体染料的强度序列（数值数组）。合成模式无需外部数据。
- **运行**：安装依赖后运行 `python begin.py`，在 GUI 中选择数据源和参数，点击运行。
- **输出**：运行结果保存在带时间戳的目录中，包含 PNG 图表和 Pickle 文件（如 `BayesFRET_data_sim_{seed}_history.p`）。
- **调试**：可参考 `code01_classes.py` 中的类定义，以及 `code02_setup.py` 中的合成数据生成逻辑。
- **GPU 需求**：无需 GPU，纯 CPU 计算。

## 核心 idea

核心洞察在于将 HDP-HMM 与实验物理模型（如光子发射率、FRET 效率）结合，通过非参数贝叶斯推断自动确定状态数，同时利用 MCMC 采样估计状态参数和转移概率，从而从噪声数据中提取 IDP 的构象动态。其创新点在于“实验信息先验”的整合，使得模型更贴合实际测量过程。

## 可搬移点

- **HDP-HMM 推断模块**（`code03_mcmc.py`）：可解耦为独立的 Python 模块，用于其他时间序列状态推断任务，如 IDP 构象系综分析。
- **合成数据生成器**（`code02_setup.py`）：可移植用于生成模拟 smFRET 数据，测试其他算法。
- **结果处理与可视化**（`code04_chart.py`、`code06_results.py`）：可复用其绘图和统计汇总逻辑。
- **GUI 框架**（`gui01_mainwindow.py`）：可作为模板，用于构建其他生物物理数据分析工具。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。
readme:
Have you ever finished [an smFRET experiment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-molecule_FRET) on [an intrinsically-disordered protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intrinsically_disordered_proteins) and wondered "What do I do with this noisy data?" Maybe you'd like to know how many configurations (conformatoinal states) your enzyme made or how those states behaved during the experiment. Then this Python app is for you! **BayesFRET** is a Python GUI program of a nonparametric Bayesian method (HDP-HMM) to estimate the number and behavior of distinct conformational states of an intrinsically-disordered molecule (ex. enzymes, Holliday junctions) from a surface-immobilized single-molecule Forster Resonance Energy Transfer (smFRET) experiment. This was originally a Ph.D.-level NSF project that became my [M.S. thesis](https://www.researchgate.net/publication/410979214_An_Experiment-Informed_Hierarchical_Dirichlet_Process-Hidden_Markov_Model_to_Analyze_Surface-Immobilized_smFRET_Data). * **Data**: Real (experimental) or mimicked (synthetic) time-binned photon intensities and experiment parameters of a molecule. Prior distributions optional. * **Method**: 4 Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) simulations on an experiment-informed Hierarchical Dirichlet Process-Hidden Markov Model (HDP-HMM). * **Results**: A directory of graphs (PNG) and numerical data (Pickle, TXT files) of simulation history and convergence. For example, an enzyme usually has at least 2 conformational states (open for business, closed for processing), but we don't know the number of states by default.​ Original work and MATLAB app were made by [Sgouralis et al](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.jpcb.8b09752). This GUI enhances and expands capabilities from the original work, taking initiative to increase the number of MCMC simulations from 1 to 4 and to increase app efficiency. # Installation 1. **Compatible Operating Systems**: Successful testing on Windows 10/11 and macOS. Untested for Linux. 1. **Python Interpreter & Environment** * Compatible versions: 3.11, 3.12, 3.13 * This documentation will assume the Python CMD call function is `python`. 1. **Download Files**: Assign a directory specifically for the files of this program (ex. `C:\Users\Cyvu37\Documents\BayesFRET`). * Make sure the parent directory of the program directory (ex. `C:\Users\Cyvu37\Documents`) doesn't require administrator access. BayesFRET must be able to produce subdirectories and files! * Processing power may vary based on the directory's location. 1. **Install Packages**: [chime](https://github.com/MaxHalford/chime), [darkdetect](https://github.com/albertosottile/darkdetect), [matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org/), [numpy](https://numpy.org/), [PySide6](https://doc.qt.io/qtforpython-6/), [scipy](https://scipy.org/) * If internet is available when BayesFRET opens, the app will auto-run the `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt` command to verify the required packages. Make sure you have [pip](https://pip.pypa.io/en/stable/installation/) and [setuptools](https://pypi.org/project/setuptools/) in your Python environment. * The app will also auto-check your Python system for the required packages and the current directory for file dependencies (ex. `code01_classes.py`). Anything missing will cause the program to close. *** **NOTE: The following content will be moved to the Wiki section.** # Before Run: The Control Panel

The program can either use data from real experiments ("Experimental") or it can run by itself using randomly generated data simulating data from an smFRET experiment ("Synthetic"). Either way, the program will run the four MCMC simulations one at a time and visualize the results. Graphs and numerical data are saved as soon as they are produced. ## Data Source Requirements * **Synthetic Mode**: None. The program generates its own data and compares it with the MCMC simulations. * **Experimental Mode** * 2 text/CSV files, each with a single array of numerical values separated by whitespace/commas. * 1 for the intensities of the *acceptor* dye throughout the experiment. * 1 for the intensities of the *donor* dye throughout the experiment. * Parameters of the experiment for the Options section of the GUI. ## GUI Features TBA ## GUI: The System Tray Icon

When opened, BayesFRET produces a system tray icon in Windows and macOS. The _Status_ and _Settings_ sections of the context menu are shortcuts to commands in the GUI. Context Menu CMD | GUI Equivalent :----------------|:---------------- Run BayesFRET | "Run" button in Settings section (when enabled) Exit BayesFRET | Closing the GUI Experimental Data: Import Donor File | Select "Experimental", then "Donor" button Experimental Data: Import Acceptor File | Select "Experimental", then "Acceptor" button Synthetic Data: Import Pickle File | Select "Synthetic - Reuse", then "Parameters + True Values" button Hide/Show Graphs During Run | Boolean to "Show Windows" checkbox Graph Size*** | Changing radio buttons in Graph Options group Randomize RNG Seeds | "Randomize!" button in RNG Seeds group Reset Settings + RNG Seeds | "Reset" button in Options section (when enabled) **Move GUI**: The commands below the _--Status--_ and _--Settings--_ sections of the context menu deal with positioning the GUI panel to one of the four corners of each active monitor in the local computer, accounting for the task bar in Windows and the menu bar in macOS. Each section corresponds to each active monitor. If you're showing graphs during a run, then these commands can move the GUI away from the open windows. **Changing Monitors**: When adding or removing an active monitor on the local computer, the GUI will automatically refresh the icon's context menu with commands for each active monitor. **Status**: During a run, hovering the mouse over the system tray icon will produce a tooltip showing the status of the program. If the icon's context menu appears during the run, the _--Status--_ header and "Run BayesFRET" command will be replaced with status messages. Moreover, the commands in the _--Settings--_ section will be disabled. ### ***Handling the Graph Size Button The 5th context menu button under _--Settings--_ may be confusing, so here are two perspectives. 1. **What It Means**: In the _Graph Options_ section of the GUI, when the radio button [A] is selected and the "Show Windows" checkbox is [B], then the text for the 5th context menu button under _--Settings--_ is [C]: A | B | C :------------|:--------------|:-------------- "1280 x 720" | enabled | "Maximize Graph Size" "1280 x 720" | disabled | "Increase Graph Size to 3200 x 1800" "Maximized" | enabled or disabled | "Decrease Graph Size to 1280 x 720" 2. **What It Does**: When the text for the 5th context menu button under _--Settings--_ is [A], selecting that button will change the radio button to [B] while keeping the "Show Windows" checkbox as [C]: A | B | C :------------|:--------------|:-------------- "Maximize Graph Size" | "Maximized" | enabled "Increase Graph Size to 3200 x 1800" | "3200 x 1800" | disabled "Decrease Graph Size to 1280 x 720" | "1280 x 720" | enabled or disabled # During Run: Running the Program When BayesFRET runs the simulations, the program stores the information inputted through the GUI into a directory with the exact timestamp of when the run started, or **the active directory**. BayesFRET uses a Universal class to store various miscellaneous data, including absolute URIs to their original directories. After the program finishes its run, data from the Universal class is saved to replicate the program's output. See the [Custom Classes](#custom-classes) section for more information. ## Avoid These Things While Running * Don't modify the BayesFRET or active directories, including their URIs and internal files, while BayesFRET runs the simulations! * Don't interact with the GUI, its windows, or the system tray icon while the simulations are running! This version doesn't support multithreading yet. # After Run: Interpreting the Results Each pickle file (`.p`) produced by this program contains data that can be instantly used in a Python environment. However, they contain custom Python classes from `code01_classes.py`. Copy `code01_classes.py` to your current directory to access the documentation of the Python classes. An advanced code editor like Visual Studio Code with extensions can provide the user with previews of documentation regarding those custom classes. ## Importing the Data The following commands import all of the data produced by a run from the program: ``` import os, pickle # Full directory path. DIR = "...{os.sep}BayesFRET_syn - 2024 04 23, 13 12 01 614687" # Import documentation. # For this line to work, you must have a copy of `code01_classes.py` in your current directory. from code01_classes import Chain_History, Params, True_Samples, Universal # Import the Universal class (`U`). with open( os.join( DIR, "BayesFRET_Universal_class.p" ), "rb" ) as file: U: Universal = pickle.load(file) # Import the parameters class (`params`). If synthetic, also import the true samples class (`TS`). with open( os.join( DIR, "BayesFRET_data_params_and_true.p" ), "rb" ) as file: if U.is_syn: X = pickle.load(file) params: Params = X[0] TS: True_Samples = X[1] else: params: Params = pickle.load(file) # Import the sampling history for each simulation (`S[0]` - `S[3]`). S: list[Chain_History] = [] FILENAMES = [os.join( DIR, "BayesFRET_data_sim_{i}_history.p" ) for i in U.list_seeds] for v in U.range_seeds: with open(FILENAMES[v], "rb") as f: S.append( pickle.load(f) ) ``` After that, you can use the variables `U`, `params`, `TS`, and `S` to your liking. ## Custom Classes * `Chain_History`: History of samples regarding key variables throughout the MCMC simulation. * Experimental + synthetic data: Found in `BayesFRET_data_sim_{i}_history.p` where `{i}` is the RNG seed value. * `Params`: Fixed parameters such as the options from the Algorithm Settings, Photoemission Priors, and Photophysics Priors sections of the GUI. * Experimental data: Found in `BayesFRET_data_params.p`. * Synthetic data: Found in `BayesFRET_data_params_and_true.p`. * `True_Samples`: Variables used in making the synthetic data from `code02_setup.py`. * Synthetic data only: Found in `BayesFRET_data_params_and_true.p`. * `Universal`: Holds all other miscellaneous variables, including... * Filenames (not filepaths) of the Chain_History pickle files (`U.filenames`).\* * List of the unique RNG seed values (`U.list_seeds`). * List of the RNG classes corresponding to each RNG seed value (`U.RNGs`). * Number of Posterior Quantiles (`U.Q`). * The full path of the active directory (`U.DIR_ACTIVE`)\* and a function to merge the path with a filename (`U.func_getActivePath(...)`).\* * The full path of the program's original directory (`U.DIR_PROGRAM`).\* \*Changes in a filename or a directory path affect these variables and functions. The following code demonstrates how to save those changes in the Universal file (`BayesFRET_Universal_class.p`). ``` # >> How to Handle Name Changes << # directory name change: DIR --> "...\BayesFRET_syn FINAL" # Filename change for 3rd seed: 'BayesFRET_data_sim_627_history.p' --> 'BayesFRET_627.p' DIR2 = "...{os.sep}BayesFRET_syn FINAL" with open( os.join( DIR2, "BayesFRET_Universal_class.p" ), "rb" ) as file: U: Universal = pickle.load(file) U.DIR_ACTIVE = DIR2 # This updates the `FILEPATH` function. U.filenames[2] = 'BayesFRET_627.p' # This allows you to use the previous for loop to iterate all filenames. ... with open(U.FILEPATH( os.join( DIR2, "BayesFRET_Universal_class.p" ) ), "wb") as file: pickle.dump( U, file ) ``` ## Usage Examples 1. Using the default RNG seeds (5, 44, 356, 9918), use the following commands to extract the FRET efficiencies `eff` of each unique state at the last MCMC iteration `n=1000` for the MCMC simulation with RNG seed 5 (`S[0]`). ``` n = 1000 # The set of unique conformational states at the MCMC iteration n=1000. ks = S[0].K_set[n] # Only extract the FRET efficiencies (`eff`) of the unique conformational states (`ks`) at n=1000. Results between 0 and 1. return S[0].eff[n, ks] ``` 2. Find the evaluated conformational states at time t (`st`) of the acceptor dye's photoemission rates $\lambda^A_{s_t}$ at the MCMC iteration `n=649` for the MCMC simulation with RNG seed 9918 (`S[3]`). ``` return S[3].lam_A[ S[3].st[649] ] ```

one_liner: Molly.jl 是一个通用分子动力学模拟的 Julia 包，支持可微模拟和多种力场，虽不专门针对 IDP/IDR 互作，但其物理模拟方法可迁移用于无序蛋白互作建模。

## 是什么
Molly.jl 是一个纯 Julia 实现的分子动力学（MD）模拟包，用于模拟从惰性气体到生物大分子的物理系统。它提供多种相互作用、积分器、恒温器、恒压器、能量最小化、副本交换、蒙特卡洛模拟等功能，并支持 GPU 加速和可微分的分子模拟。

## 亮点
- **纯 Julia 实现**：无需外部依赖，易于安装和扩展，与 Julia 生态无缝集成。
- **可微分模拟**：这是该包独有的特性，支持通过自动微分计算能量和力的梯度，可用于力场参数优化和机器学习。
- **模块化设计**：允许用户自定义相互作用、模拟器、恒温器、日志器等，灵活性高。
- **多后端 GPU 支持**：通过 KernelAbstractions.jl 支持所有后端，包括 CUDA，但当前性能比 OpenMM 慢约 5 倍。
- **丰富的力场和文件格式支持**：可读取 OpenMM 力场 XML 文件，支持 Chemfiles.jl 读取和写入多种坐标/轨迹格式（如 PDB、DCD、XTC）。
- **内置多种高级模拟方法**：副本交换分子动力学（REMD）、蒙特卡洛模拟、AWH 和 TSS 自由能计算方法。

## 为何对本课题有用
Molly.jl 直接适用于 IDR/IDP 的分子动力学模拟，尤其是其**可微分模拟**特性，可用于开发针对无序蛋白的力场（如论文中所述）。它支持隐式溶剂模型（GBSA），适合模拟无序蛋白的构象系综。此外，其模块化设计允许集成机器学习势（如 ANI），可用于构建无序蛋白的语言模型或混合 AI/物理模拟。对于 LLPS 研究，其副本交换和自由能计算工具可用于采样相分离相关的构象和结合自由能。

## 怎么用
- **安装**：需要 Julia v1.10+，在 Julia REPL 中按 `]` 进入包模式，运行 `add Molly`。GPU 支持需额外安装如 `CUDA` 的包。
- **主入口**：`src/Molly.jl` 是主模块，示例代码在 README 中，包括 Lennard-Jones 流体和蛋白质模拟。
- **输入/输出**：输入可以是原子坐标（如 PDB 文件）和力场文件（OpenMM XML），输出轨迹文件（DCD、XTC）和日志。
- **GPU 加速**：需要 GPU 时，使用 `CuArray` 作为 `array_type`，并安装相应后端。
- **测试**：`test/` 目录包含大量单元测试，如 `test/simulation_1.jl`、`test/gradients_1.jl` 等，可用于调试和验证。
- **文档**：`docs/src/` 包含详细文档，特别是 `docs/src/differentiable.md` 和 `docs/src/free_energy.md` 对可微分模拟和自由能方法有深入说明。

## 核心 idea
Molly.jl 的核心创新在于**将分子动力学模拟与自动微分结合**，使得模拟过程可微分，从而能够通过梯度下降优化力场参数或学习势能函数。这种设计打破了传统 MD 模拟的不可微限制，为数据驱动的力场开发和 AI 辅助模拟提供了新范式。

## 可搬移点
- **可微分模拟框架**：`src/force.jl` 和 `src/energy.jl` 中的能量/力计算支持自动微分，可提取用于自定义的力场优化 Pipeline。
- **模块化相互作用接口**：`src/interactions/` 下的各种相互作用实现（如 Lennard-Jones、Coulomb）可独立复用，便于替换或扩展。
- **自由能计算模块**：`src/free_energy/` 中的 AWH、TSS 和 MBAR 实现可用于构象系综的采样和自由能估计。
- **邻居列表和 PME 实现**：`src/neighbors.jl` 和 `src/interactions/ewald.jl` 中的高效算法可移植到其他模拟代码中。
- **许可证**：MIT 许可证（见 LICENSE.md），允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体条款。

![Molly logo](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/master/docs/src/images/logo_molly.svg)

[![Build status](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/actions)
[![Coverage status](https://codecov.io/gh/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/branch/master/graph/badge.svg?token=RD9XF0W90L)](https://codecov.io/gh/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl)
[![Latest release](https://img.shields.io/github/release/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl.svg)](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/releases/latest)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green.svg)](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/blob/master/LICENSE.md)
[![Documentation stable](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-stable-blue.svg)](https://JuliaMolSim.github.io/Molly.jl/stable)
[![Documentation dev](https://img.shields.io/badge/docs-dev-blue.svg)](https://JuliaMolSim.github.io/Molly.jl/dev)

Much of science can be explained by the movement and interaction of molecules.
Molecular dynamics (MD) is a computational technique used to explore these phenomena, from noble gases to biological macromolecules.
Molly.jl is a pure Julia package for MD, and for the simulation of physical systems more broadly.

The package is described in [a talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XTE5HSo-jx8) at JuliaCon 2024, [an earlier talk](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6G97jDVPlYc) at Enzyme Conference 2023 and [a tutorial](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rVRWIxLyjgE) at the MolSSI JuliaMolSim Workshop 2024.
[Slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1CvGwFn0XjiIfAQ562RlIPGjXRKnsNXLYjmPRDFS7SQs/edit?usp=sharing) are also available for a tutorial in 2025.

Implemented features include:
- Non-bonded interactions - Lennard-Jones van der Waals/repulsion force, electrostatic Coulomb potential and reaction field, gravitational potential, soft sphere potential, Mie potential, Buckingham potential, soft core variants for alchemical simulation.
- Bonded interactions - harmonic and Morse bonds, bond angles, torsion angles, harmonic position restraints, FENE bonds.
- Ewald and particle mesh Ewald (PME) electrostatic summation.
- Interface to allow definition of new interactions, simulators, thermostats, loggers etc.
- Read in OpenMM force field files and coordinate files supported by [Chemfiles.jl](https://github.com/chemfiles/Chemfiles.jl).
- Write out trajectory files in formats supported by Chemfiles.jl, including DCD and XTC.
- Verlet, velocity Verlet, Störmer-Verlet, flexible Langevin, Nosé-Hoover and multiple time stepping integrators.
- Andersen, Berendsen and velocity rescaling thermostats.
- C-rescale, Monte Carlo and Berendsen barostats with flexible virial calculation.
- Steepest descent, FIRE and L-BFGS energy minimization.
- Replica exchange molecular dynamics.
- Monte Carlo simulation.
- Periodic, triclinic and infinite boundary conditions.
- Constraints with SHAKE and RATTLE.
- Virtual sites.
- Flexible loggers to track arbitrary properties throughout simulations.
- Cutoff and mixing algorithms for non-bonded interactions.
- Various neighbor list implementations to speed up the calculation of non-bonded forces, including the use of [CellListMap.jl](https://github.com/m3g/CellListMap.jl).
- Implicit solvent GBSA methods.
- [Unitful.jl](https://github.com/PainterQubits/Unitful.jl) compatibility so numbers have physical meaning.
- Set up crystal systems using [SimpleCrystals.jl](https://github.com/ejmeitz/SimpleCrystals.jl).
- Flexible bias potentials and collective variables.
- Native support for the [ANI](https://github.com/aiqm/torchani) machine learning interatomic potential.
- Automatic multithreading.
- GPU acceleration on all backends supported by [KernelAbstractions.jl](https://github.com/JuliaGPU/KernelAbstractions.jl), with better performance on CUDA-enabled devices.
- Run with Float64, Float32 or other float types.
- Some analysis functions, e.g. RDF.
- Visualise simulations as animations with [Makie.jl](https://makie.juliaplots.org/stable).
- Compatibility with [AtomsBase.jl](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/AtomsBase.jl) and [AtomsCalculators.jl](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/AtomsCalculators.jl).
- Interface to use Python [ASE](https://ase-lib.org) calculators.
- Control of random numbers during simulation, allowing reproducible stochastic simulations.
- Differentiable molecular simulation. This is a unique feature of the package and the focus of its current development.

Features not yet implemented include:
- Optimal GPU performance - currently we are ~5x slower than OpenMM on CUDA GPUs.
- Protein preparation - solvent box, add hydrogens etc.
- Simulators such as metadynamics.
- Quantum mechanical modelling.
- Domain decomposition algorithms.

## Installation

[Julia](https://julialang.org/downloads) is required, with Julia v1.10 or later required to get the latest version of Molly.
It is recommended to run on the current stable Julia release for the best performance.
Install Molly from the Julia REPL.
Enter the package mode by pressing `]` and run `add Molly`.
If you want to run on a GPU you will also need to install the appropriate package for your system, e.g. `add CUDA`.

## Usage

Some examples are given here, see [the documentation](https://juliamolsim.github.io/Molly.jl/stable/documentation) for more on how to use the package.

Simulation of a Lennard-Jones fluid:
```julia
using Molly

n_atoms = 100
boundary = CubicBoundary(2.0u"nm")
temp = 298.0u"K"
atom_mass = 10.0u"g/mol"

atoms = [Atom(mass=atom_mass, σ=0.3u"nm", ϵ=0.2u"kJ * mol^-1") for i in 1:n_atoms]
coords = place_atoms(n_atoms, boundary; min_dist=0.3u"nm")
velocities = [random_velocity(atom_mass, temp) for i in 1:n_atoms]
pairwise_inters = (LennardJones(),)

simulator = VelocityVerlet(
    dt=0.002u"ps",
    coupling=AndersenThermostat(temp, 1.0u"ps"),
)

sys = System(
    atoms=atoms,
    coords=coords,
    boundary=boundary,
    velocities=velocities,
    pairwise_inters=pairwise_inters,
    loggers=(temp=TemperatureLogger(100),),
)

simulate!(sys, simulator, 10_000)
```

Simulation of a protein on GPU:
```julia
using Molly, CUDA

data_dir = joinpath(dirname(pathof(Molly)), "..", "data")
T = Float32
ff = MolecularForceField(
    T,
    joinpath(data_dir, "force_fields", "ff99SBildn.xml"),
    joinpath(data_dir, "force_fields", "tip3p_standard.xml"),
)

sys = System(
    joinpath(data_dir, "6mrr_equil.pdb"),
    ff;
    nonbonded_method=:pme,
    loggers=(
        energy=TotalEnergyLogger(10),
        writer=TrajectoryWriter(10, "traj_6mrr_5ps.dcd"),
    ),
    array_type=CuArray,
)

minimizer = SteepestDescentMinimizer()
simulate!(sys, minimizer)

temp = T(298.0)u"K"
random_velocities!(sys, temp)
simulator = Langevin(
    dt=T(0.001)u"ps",
    temperature=temp,
    friction=T(1.0)u"ps^-1",
    coupling=MonteCarloBarostat(T(1.0)u"bar", temp, sys.boundary),
)

simulate!(sys, simulator, 5_000)
```
The above 5 ps simulation looks something like this when you view it in PyMOL:
![MD simulation](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/raw/master/docs/src/images/sim_6mrr.gif)

## Contributing

Contributions are very welcome including reporting bugs, fixing bugs, adding new features, improving performance, adding tests and improving documentation.
Feel free to open an issue or use the channels below to discuss your contribution.
New features will generally require tests to be added as well.
As described in the documentation, potentials implementing the [AtomsCalculators](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/AtomsCalculators.jl) interface can be used with Molly.
If you have an interesting example of such a potential in your package, do contribute an example to the Molly documentation.
See the [roadmap issue](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/issues/2) for some discussion of recent progress and future plans.

Join the #molly channel on the [JuliaMolSim Zulip](https://juliamolsim.zulipchat.com/join/j5sqhiajbma5hw55hy6wtzv7), the #juliamolsim channel on the [Julia Slack](https://join.slack.com/t/julialang/shared_invite/zt-26arhonkh-WYNI2rI2X85jcbkn6pRAjA) or post on the [Julia Discourse](https://discourse.julialang.org) to discuss the usage and development of Molly.jl.

Molly.jl follows the Contributor Covenant [code of conduct](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/blob/master/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

## Citation

If you use Molly, please cite the following paper ([bib entry here](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/blob/master/CITATION.bib), [cff entry here](https://github.com/JuliaMolSim/Molly.jl/blob/master/CITATION.cff)):

## 是什么

这是一个精选论文与工具列表仓库（awesome-list），系统收集了**分子构象**（小分子、RNA、肽、蛋白质、酶、抗体、蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用等）与**分子动力学/力场**相关的生成式 AI 与深度学习研究。它本身不提供代码，而是作为该领域的导航索引，帮助研究者快速定位最新方法、数据集与软件包。

## 亮点

- **覆盖面广**：从量子化学、从头算 MD 到粗粒化力场、神经力场、增强采样、轨迹分析，几乎涵盖分子模拟全链条。
- **分类清晰**：按方法（扩散、Flow、VAE、GAN、Transformer 等）与分子类型（小分子、RNA、肽、蛋白等）双重维度组织，便于检索。
- **持续更新**：标注“Updating...”，收录了 2024-2026 年的最新工作，时效性强。
- **附带资源**：不仅列论文，还收录了数据集（如 mdCATH、nablaDFT）与软件包（如 MMolearn、MDAnalysis），可直接用于实践。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题聚焦**固有无序蛋白（IDR/IDP）**的构象系综、互作与相分离。该列表直接提供了大量相关资源：

- **构象系综生成**：列表中的生成模型（扩散、Flow、VAE 等）可用于生成 IDP 的多样构象，解决实验难以捕捉的系综问题。
- **力场与模拟**：神经力场（如 MACE-OFF、Grappa）和增强采样方法（如 metadynamics）可提升 IDP 模拟的精度与采样效率。
- **数据集**：mdCATH 等大规模 MD 数据集可作为训练 IDP 构象预测模型的基准。
- **互作建模**：PPI 构象动力学相关条目可迁移至 IDP 介导的互作研究。
- **工具链**：轨迹分析工具（MDAnalysis、MDTraj）与可视化工具可直接用于 IDP 系综分析。

## 怎么用

- **入口**：直接浏览仓库的 README.md，按目录跳转到感兴趣的分类。
- **安装**：无需安装，纯索引。
- **数据格式**：各条目链接到原始论文或代码仓库，数据格式因项目而异（如 PDB、FASTA、HDF5 等）。
- **调试**：无代码可调试，但可点击链接进入具体项目，获取可运行的 Demo 或测试。
- **GPU**：取决于具体项目，多数深度学习模型需要 GPU。

## 核心 idea

该仓库的核心价值在于**系统化梳理**：将分散的论文、代码、数据整合为结构化索引，使研究者能快速定位“哪个方法解决哪个问题”，从而避免重复调研，加速科研选题与方案设计。

## 可搬移点

- **分类体系**：其“方法 × 分子类型”的二维分类法可直接借鉴，用于构建自己的文献管理或工具导航系统。
- **资源清单**：可直接引用其中的数据集（如 mdCATH）和工具（如 MMolearn）作为自己 Pipeline 的组件。
- **License**：仓库本身为 GPL 许可，但各条目资源许可需逐一确认。

> 注意：本仓库为索引，不提供代码，因此“可搬移点”更多是资源与组织方式的借鉴。

### MD Engines-Frameworks

* [Amber](http://ambermd.org/) - A suite of biomolecular simulation programs.  
* [Gromacs](http://www.gromacs.org/) - A molecular dynamics package mainly designed for simulations of proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
* [OpenMM](http://openmm.org/) - A toolkit for molecular simulation using high performance GPU code.  
* [CHARMM](https://www.charmm.org/) - A molecular simulation program with broad application to many-particle systems.  
* [HTMD](https://github.com/Acellera/htmd) - Programming Environment for Molecular Discovery.  
* [ACEMD](https://www.acellera.com/acemd) - The next generation molecular dynamic simulation software.  
* [NAMD](https://www.ks.uiuc.edu/Research/namd/) - A parallel molecular dynamics code for large biomolecular systems.
* [StreaMD](https://github.com/ci-lab-cz/streamd) - A tool to perform high-throughput automated molecular dynamics simulations.
* [BEMM-GEN](https://github.com/y4suda/BEMM-GEN) - A Toolkit for Generating a Biomolecular Environment-Mimicking Model for Molecular Dynamics Simulation.
* [BioSimSpace](https://github.com/OpenBioSim/biosimspace) - An interoperable Python framework for biomolecular simulation.
* [STORMM](https://github.com/Psivant/stormm) - Structure and TOpology Replica Molecular Mechanics.
* [multiSMD](https://github.com/kszewc/multiSMD) - A Python Toolset for Multidirectional Steered Molecular Dynamics.
* [CCD2MD](https://github.com/keb721/CCD2MD) - A Suite of Packages for Preparing Co-Folded Outputs for Molecular Dynamics Simulations.

one_liner: 该仓库是MAVISp癌症突变注释流程的Snakemake自动化管道，包含IDP/IDR专用目标规则，但核心面向突变效应预测而非无序蛋白互作机制建模。
card:
## 是什么

MAVISp_automatization 是一个基于 Snakemake 的自动化流水线，用于执行 MAVISp 框架中的多个步骤，包括元数据生成、突变聚合、AlphaFold 模型获取与修剪、PDB 信息检索、互作信息获取、磷酸化预测、RaSP 稳定性计算、突变分类、早期折叠区域预测等，最终生成用于 MAVISp 分析的输入文件。

## 亮点

- **高度模块化**：通过 Snakemake 将多个独立工具（cancermuts、pdbminer、RaSP、NetPhos、RosettaDDGprediction、EFoldMine 等）串联成自动化流程，便于扩展和替换。
- **针对 IDP 的专用目标规则**：提供 `idps` 和 `essentials_idps` 目标，跳过结构相关的昂贵计算，适用于固有无序蛋白。
- **灵活的配置**：通过 YAML 配置文件指定各工具路径和环境，适应不同计算环境。
- **输出组织清晰**：每个蛋白一个文件夹，包含所有中间结果和最终汇总，便于追踪和调试。

## 为何对本课题有用

该流水线直接面向癌症结构生物学中的突变效应分析，但其设计思路和工具集成方式对 IDR/IDP 研究具有高度可迁移性：
- **IDP 专用目标**：`idps` 规则展示了如何为无序蛋白定制分析流程，跳过结构依赖的步骤，这对 IDP 构象系综和互作研究非常关键。
- **互作信息聚合**：从 Mentha、STRING、hpc-atlas 等数据库获取互作数据，可用于 IDP 介导的互作网络分析。
- **磷酸化预测**：NetPhos 和 de novo 磷酸化位点识别，可用于研究 IDP 中磷酸化调控的突变效应。
- **早期折叠预测**：EFoldMine 预测早期折叠区域，有助于识别 IDP 中的局部结构倾向。
- **稳定性计算**：RaSP 和 Rosetta 的集成可用于评估突变对蛋白稳定性的影响，尽管对 IDP 可能不适用，但可借鉴其自动化流程。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：Snakefile 位于仓库根目录，通过 `snakemake -c 1` 运行（默认目标），或 `snakemake -c 1 idps` 运行 IDP 目标。
- **安装与依赖**：需要 Python 3.10 及 pandas、os、re、shutil、glob、datetime 等包；外部工具包括 cancermuts、pdbminer、RaSP、NetPhos、demask、RosettaDDGprediction、efoldmine、procheck；数据库包括 mentha、AlphaFold2、hpc-atlas、Alphamissense、AF_Huri。
- **输入数据**：CSV 文件（包含蛋白名、UniProt ID、修剪范围、参考序列等列），以及 mavisp_templates 脚本目录和 config.yaml 配置文件。
- **输出数据**：每个蛋白一个文件夹，包含 AlphaFold 模型、PDB 信息、互作数据、突变列表、稳定性结果等。
- **调试示例**：仓库提供 `example/` 目录，包含标准、essentials、idps 等不同模式的示例，可直接运行或断点调试。
- **GPU 需求**：README 未说明，但 RaSP 和 Rosetta 可能支持 GPU，需根据具体环境配置。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于**将复杂的多步骤生物信息学分析流程抽象为可配置、可复用的 Snakemake 流水线**，通过模块化设计实现不同蛋白（包括 IDP）的自动化分析，同时保持灵活性和可扩展性。

## 可搬移点

- **IDP 目标规则**：`idps` 和 `essentials_idps` 的 Snakemake 规则定义，可直接借鉴用于构建 IDP 专属分析流程，跳过结构计算。
- **互作数据聚合模块**：`interactome/` 下的脚本（如 mentha2pdb.py、aggregate）可解耦用于从多个数据库获取和整合互作信息。
- **突变列表生成模块**：`cancermuts/` 下的脚本可独立用于从不同数据库聚合突变数据。
- **早期折叠预测模块**：`efoldmine/` 的调用逻辑可移植到自定义 Pipeline 中。
- **配置管理**：config.yaml 的设计模式可复用于管理多工具路径和环境。
- **License**：README 未说明，需确认。

# Mavisp automatization pipeline

Cancer Structural Biology, Danish Cancer Society Research Center, 2100, Copenhagen, Denmark

Cancer Systems Biology, Health and Technology Department, Section for Bioinformatics, 2800, Lyngby, Denmark

## Introduction

MAVISp_automatization is a Snakemake pipeline that has been designed to automate the various steps involved in the mavisp framework. With this pipeline, users are able to perform the following tasks automatically: 
- generation of metadata relative to each protein and the curator,
- mutations aggregation, 
- retrieval and trimming of PDB models from AplphaFold ,
- retrieval information of all available PDBs in the Protein Data Bank, 
- filtering of mutation lists for further calculations,
- retrieval and aggregation of interaction information through two different databases,  
- protein phosphorylation prediction,
- RaSP calculation,
- classification of mutations occurring in protein sequence through different approaches,
- identification of denovo phosphorylation sites upon mutation
- early folding regions prediction
- relevant data collection to be used by mavisp.py

it also contains an alternative target rule (`idps`) that generate targets for
intrisically disordered proteins, therefore skipping expensive calculations on
the structure that wouldn't be appropriate for such cases.

## Requirements

### Required software

The pipeline uses the following Python packages:

- pandas
- os
- re
- shutil
- glob
- datetime

The pipeline requires the following programs:
- cancermuts
- pdbminer
- rasp
- netphos
- demask
- RosettaDDGprediction
- efoldmine
- procheck

The pipeline requires the following databases:
- mentha
- AlphaFold2
- hpc-atlas
- Alphamissense
- AF_Huri

It also requires to have a full mutational scan performed using MutateX.

Before running the pipeline, please ensure that all the requirements are met.

### Input structure

The pipeline necessitates a CSV input file, a folder containing the scripts essential for the MAVISP framework (mavisp_templates), and a config.yaml file specifying the locations of the scripts essential for the pipeline. The input file, 'input.csv,' and the scripts directory should reside in the same directory as the Snakefile (an example is provided in the repository). The CSV file should encompass the subsequent comma-separated columns:

|protein|uniprot_ac|uniprot_id|trimmed|ref_seq|research_field|input_pdb|structure_source|model|curator_name|affiliation|
|-------|----------|----------|-------|-------|--------------|---------|----------------|-----|------------|-----------|
|BLM|P54132|BLM_HUMAN|1-359_368-1290|NP_000048|vus||AF2|v4|Elena Papaleo_Pablo Sanchez-Izquierdo|"DTU, Denmark; DCI, Denmark_DTU, Denmark; DCI, Denmark"|

where:
"protein" is the hugo name of the protein
"uniprot_id" is the uniprot id of the protein
"uniprot_ac" is the uniprot accession number of the protein
"trimmed" represents the residues range of your trimmed model (in case of multiple models specify the ranges "_" separeted)
"ref_seq" is the ref seq code associated with the isoform used by cancermuts (usually the first one). The RefSeq associated with the first isoform can be accessed through the Uniprot database in the "Sequence & isoforms" or "Sequence" section (depending on the protein being investigated) under the field "Sequence databases". The RefSeq code required by the pipeline consists of the "NP" followed by all subsequent characters until the dot, excluding it. There may be multiple RefSeq codes available. The one associated with the correct isoform includes the isoform code, which is enclosed in square brackets, corresponding to the canonical isoform. Verify by clicking on it that it corresponds to the correct isoform.
"research_field" is the project or the research field in which the protein is involved (this is the name of the folder in which the cancermuts and rasp calculation will be organized).
"input_pdb" is an optional input pdb file the user provides. Notice that this is mandatory when using the `idp` rule target.
"structure_source" the source of the input structure, it needs to follow the nameing of this dictionary:
AFDB: "AlphaFold database",
AF3: "AlphaFold3 webserver",
AF2: "AlphaFold2 standalone",
PDB: "Experimental PDB structure",
Mod: "Homology model (PDB template, reconstruction)
"model" is the model of the structure used (vX)
An additional and optional input file in txt format containing the mutations from other sources than COSMIC, cBioPortal, and Clinvar can be provided. The mutations will be aggregated along with all the mutations found in the afromentioned databases by cancermuts in the metatable. This file name must start with the hugo name of the protein in capital letters and end with .txt extension (i.e BLM_my_mutation_list.txt); the mutations must be reported in one letter code as reported below without header
A34P
C56Y
Y678L
"curator_name" is the names of the curators that have worked in the curation of the protein (in case of multiple curators specify the names "_" separated).
"affiliation" is the organitation/s where the curator is affiliated to (in case of multiple curators specify the affiliations "_" separated in the same order as where introduced the curators). Put this whole field between comas ("affiliation1_affiliation2") to avoid parsing issues.

### Configfile.yaml
The pipeline supports a configuration file in the yaml format allowing customization of the script location and the environment settings required by the various software utilized in the pipeline. Below is an example of a configuration file:

```
input:
    path: input.csv
modules:
    interactome:
        mentha2pdb:
            database_date: 2025-04-28
            database_path: /data/databases/mentha-20250428
            AF_Huri_path:  /data/databases/AF_Huri_HuMAP/summary/huri_upac.csv
            AF_HuMAP_path: /data/databases/AF_Huri_HuMAP/summary/humap_upac.csv
            AF_Huri_HuMAP_path: /data/databases/AF_Huri_HuMAP
        hpc_atlas:
            database_path: /data/databases/hpc_atlas/HPC-Atlas_gene.txt
    structure_selection:
        alphafold:
            dssp_exec: /usr/local/dssp-3.0.10/bin/mkdssp
        pdbminer:
            pdbminer_env: . /usr/local/envs/PDBminer/bin/activate
        procheck:
            procheck_env: export prodir=/usr/local/procheck && export PATH=$PATH:$prodir
    mutations_classifier:
        demask:
            source: /usr/local/envs/demask/demask_env/bin/activate 
            database_path: /data/databases/uniref90demask/uniref90demask
            blastp_path: /usr/local/blast_plus-2.13.0/bin/blastp
        alphamissense:
            database_path: /data/databases/alphamissense/AlphaMissense_aa_substitutions.tsv.gz 
    mutations_aggregation:
        cancermuts:
            source: /usr/local/envs/cancermuts/bin/activate
            Cosmic_database_path: /data/databases/cosmic-v96/CosmicMutantExport.tsv
            template_path: /data/raw_data/computational_data/cancermuts_testing/mavisp_templates_final/pancancer.py
            saturation: true
            ELM_connections_per_run: 1
            folder_name: /data/raw_data/computational_data/cancermuts_testing/
        mutlist:
            source: . /usr/local/envs/cancermuts/bin/activate
    rasp: 
        conda_activation: /usr/local/miniconda3/bin/activate
        rasp_conda_env: /usr/local/envs/RaSP_workflow
        output_path_folder: /data/raw_data/computational_data/rasp_testing/
        folder_name: rasp
    rosetta_relax:
        rosetta_env: /usr/local/envs/rosettaddgprediction/bin/activate
        rosetta_module: /usr/local/rosetta-2022.11/
        rosetta_folder:  /data/raw_data/computational_data/rosetta_testing/
        rosetta_template: /data/raw_data/computational_data/rosetta_data/mavisp_templates/stability/ref2015_cartesian2020
    efoldmine:
        environment: set +eu && . /usr/local/envs/efoldmine/bin/activate && set -eu
```

Before running the pipeline, please ensure that you customize the configuration file by providing the correct paths for the environment, databases and the location of the cancermuts script template.
N.B the field ELM_connections_per_run specifiy the number of cancermuts run that can be run in parallell. It's essential to query ELM database once at time, for this reason the parameter needs to be set 1. 
N.B The template files for the RasP calculations are collected in the following path: 

```
/data/raw_data/computational_data/rasp_data/mavisp_templates/free/AF2_XX-YY/model_vX/
```

## Workflow

The pipeline automates the following steps for each entry in the input CSV file, collecting the corresponding readouts and organizing them into specific folders based on the HUGO name of each entry (refer to the example folder):

- **Retrieving and trimming AlphaFold models**: The associated PDB file for each entry in the input file is copied from MutateX folder. Each trimmed model is stored in the "structure_selection/original_model/" path (see example folder). Only regions with high pLDDT scores are retained. The residue range is used in subsequent steps to filter the mutation list for calculations. 
For proteins using experimental PDB or any other custom structure, the specified PDB file is copied from working directory and trimmed as needed.
Notice that when using the `idps` target rule, the PDB file always needs to be specified manually, as the MutateX run will not be available.

- **Retrieving available PDB information through PDB miner**: Information about all possible experimental structures available in the Protein Data Bank (PDB), such as resolution, 
  experimental method, and missing residues, is collected for each entry in the input file. The readouts are stored in the "structure_selection/pdbminer/" path.
    
- **Filtering PDB miner results**: Complexes extracted by PDB miner are filtered based on a 10 Å interaction distance. Only complexes meeting this criterion are retained, and their binding interface residues are extracted. If available, the PDB structures of these complexes are downloaded. The readouts are stored in the "structure_selection/pdbminer_complexes/" folder. 

- **Running Procheck for Structure Quality Assessment**: The Procheck tool is used to assess the quality of the trimmed AlphaFold models. This analysis generates summary files that provide detailed information about the stereochemical quality of the trimmed models generated in the previous step, including Ramachandran plot statistics. The readouts are stored in the "structure_selection/procheck/" folder.

- **Cancermuts step**: The pipeline aggregates cancer mutations from cBioPortal, COSMIC, and ClinVar databases, along with structural information (SLiMs, secondary structure, Post Translational Modification sites PTMs) of the protein. In case multiple entrez IDs are found for one protein, no gene ID will be assigned and mutation retrieval from cBioPortal will be skipped. The output is stored in a path specified in the config.yaml file.

- **Creation of MutateX, Rosetta, and CabsFlex compatible mutation lists**: Using the "metatable.csv" file from the cancermuts output and the residue range from the trimmed model, 
  mutation lists are created in the appropriate format for the following calculations: protein stability through the FoldX energy function (MutateX), protein stability through the Rosetta energy function Ref2015, and conformational structural ensemble generation of mutants and WT through CabsFlex (used with the ensemble mode). Additionally, a mutation list with potential phospho residues for the MutateX calculation is created. Also, mutation lists containing mutations occurring at positions annotated as glycosylated in the cancermuts metatable (O-, N-, C-, and S-linked) are generated. Finally, a mutation list with mutations expressed in one-letter code is created for other annotation steps. The files are stored in the "cancermuts" folder.

- **Domain annotations based on the mutation list**: The mutation list obtained in the previous step is used to retrieve information about the domains in the protein under investigation. 
  The readouts are stored in the "structure_selection/domain_annotations/" path.

- **Retrieving interactors from the Mentha database**: Information about experimentally validated interactors collected in the Mentha and database is retrieved and organized in a CSV file, 
  along with information about possible PDB IDs and associated PMID references. Each interactor is assigned a score indicating the certainty of the interaction. The output is stored in the "interactome/mentha2pdb" path.

- **Retrieving interactors from the STRING database**: Interactors are extracted from the physical subnetwork of STRING, keeping only those with a score > 0.15 and supported by either curated database annotations or experimental data. Available PDBs of the retrieved complexes are included. Output is stored in "interactome/string2pdb".

- **Retrieving interactors from the hpc-atlas database**: Interactor information collected in the hpc-atlas database is retrieved and organized into a txt file. The file is stored in the 
  "interactome/hpc_atlas" path.

- **Aggregating retrieved interaction data**: Interactors that have been extracted from STRING or Mentha, along with the structures of their complexes with the target protein obtained from PDBminer or PDBMiner_coplexes tools are aggregated in a single csv file. Output is stored in "interactome/aggregate".

- **Mutation classification using the Demask approach**: The uniprot fasta file, automatically retrieved by the pipeline, is provided to the Demask software to obtain a classification for 
  every possible mutation at each sequence position. The output is stored in the "demask" folder.

- **Mutation classification using the Alphamissense approach**: The uniprot_ac, automatically retrieved by the pipeline, is used to filter the Alphamissense file to obtain a classification for 
  every possible mutation at each sequence position. The output is stored in the "alphamissense" folder.

- **Rasp calculation on trimmed models**: The trimmed models obtained in the previous step are provided to the Rasp workflow to obtain stability effect predictions for every possible 
  mutation at each sequence position. The output is stored in the same folder as the "rasp_data" Snakefile.

- **Protein phosphorylation predictions using NetPhos**: The NetPhos software is used to predict phosphorylatable residues in the protein sequence, along with the corresponding kinases 
  responsible for the phosphorylation and their associated confidence scores. The output is stored in the "netphos" folder.

- **RosettaDDGprediction relax step**: The Cartesian2020 protocol and the ref2015 energy function from the Rosetta suite are exploited to perform the relax step required by the software using the trimmed structure obtained in the step above. The output is stored in a path specified in the config.yaml file.

- **identification of denovo phosphorylation sites**: netphos is used on wild-type or mutant sequences to identify cases in which mutations cause significant changes in the propensity of a certain site to be phosphorylated

- **Prediction of early folding sites**: EFoldMine is employed in order to predict regions with early folding propensity from the target protein's primary sequence, so that it can be subsequently identified whether the mutation sites of the investigated variants fall within the predicted early folding regions. The EFoldMine output is stored in the "efoldmine/" folder.

- **Metadata generation step**: All the relevant information of the curation of each protein for each run is stored in "metadata" folder.

- **Output collection**: The most relevant outputs from all the steps are collected in one single folder that will be further used to automatically generate the mavisp.csv. The output is stored in the "simple_mode" folder.  

## Output structure

## Usage

In order to run the pipeline (see example folder):

```
conda deactivate

module load python/3.10

snakemake -c 1
```

to use the target rule for IDPs, instead:

## 是什么
AnHydra（仓库/包名 `tardiscreen`）是一个针对蛋白质序列的**家族分类与分诊工具**，用于判断给定序列是否属于已知的耐干燥保护性蛋白家族（如 CAHS、LEA、dehydrin）。它通过 ESM-2 蛋白语言模型提取嵌入，并训练一个轻量分类器，同时提供一个可解释的平行生物物理模型和基于 Gemini 的通俗语言解释。它明确声明不是功效预测器，而是回答“该序列是否属于这些保护性家族”。

## 亮点
- **严谨的评估设计**：采用 CD-HIT 40% 序列聚类划分的 5 折交叉验证，避免行级泄漏；并额外进行“整家族留出”测试，揭示 BLAST 与 ESM-2 在泛化上的差异。
- **可解释性**：除黑盒 ESM-2 分类器外，还训练了一个从零开始的 CNN，并从中提取出 48 个 motif，其中多个与已发表的 dehydrin K-segment 一致，实现了“模型自发现已知生物学 motif”。
- **对抗混淆的自我审查**：主动识别并修复了“无序性”这一主要混淆变量，通过 caliper 匹配（Austin 2011）构建了与阳性样本在无序覆盖度和长度上平衡的阴性集。
- **轻量部署**：ESM-2 小模型可在 CPU 上运行，无需 GPU，适合快速部署和演示。
- **模块化流水线**：数据获取、阴性构建、特征提取、模型训练、评估、解释各步骤分离，便于复用和调试。

## 为何对本课题有用
该仓库直接针对 **IDR/IDP × 分子互作 × 计算与 AI** 课题中的核心问题：如何从序列中识别具有特定功能（耐干燥保护）的无序蛋白。其方法学可迁移到其他 IDP 功能分类任务，例如预测相分离驱动蛋白或分子伴侣。
- **无序蛋白语言模型**：展示了如何利用冻结的 ESM-2 嵌入进行下游分类，并验证了其在“整家族留出”场景下的泛化能力，这对构建 IDP 功能预测器有直接参考价值。
- **可解释性**：CNN motif 提取方法可迁移到发现新的 IDP 功能 motif，例如相分离相关的重复序列或相互作用基序。
- **混淆控制**：其处理“无序性”混淆变量的方法（caliper 匹配）对任何 IDP 相关分类任务都至关重要，因为无序性本身可能掩盖真正的功能信号。
- **生物物理特征**：9 个可解释特征（如无序覆盖度、长度等）可作为 IDP 构象系综或互作建模的辅助特征。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`app/main.py` 提供 FastAPI 服务，接收序列并返回分数和解释。数据流水线入口为 `src/tardiscreen/data.py`，模型训练入口为 `src/tardiscreen/model.py`。
- **安装**：`pip install -e ".[ml]"` 安装完整模型栈（torch, transformers, scikit-learn）。需要外部工具 CD-HIT 用于聚类。
- **运行**：复制 `.env.example` 为 `.env`，设置 `APP_ENV=development` 和 `AUTH_DEV_ANONYMOUS=true` 可本地运行。启动服务：`uvicorn app.main:app --env-file .env --host 127.0.0.1 --reload`。
- **数据格式**：输入为蛋白质序列（20–1022 个标准残基，可含 FASTA 头）。输出为分类分数和解释文本。
- **测试**：`tests/` 目录包含单元测试，可运行 `pytest` 进行调试。
- **GPU 需求**：README 说明 ESM-2 小模型可在 CPU 上运行，无需 GPU。

## 核心 idea
核心方法学洞察是：**通过对比“保护性无序蛋白”与“其他无序蛋白”来消除无序性本身的混淆，从而让模型学习真正的功能信号**。这通过 caliper 匹配实现，并辅以整家族留出评估来验证泛化。此外，CNN motif 提取展示了如何从黑盒模型中提取可解释的生物学知识，为 IDP 功能研究提供了“模型即发现工具”的思路。

## 可搬移点
- **阴性集构建与匹配逻辑**（`src/tardiscreen/build_negatives.py`, `match_negatives.py`）：可直接复制用于任何 IDP 功能分类任务，以控制无序性混淆。
- **CNN motif 提取**（`src/tardiscreen/cnn.py`, `motifs.py`）：可迁移到发现新的 IDP 功能 motif，例如相分离相关序列。
- **评估框架**（`src/tardiscreen/evaluate.py`, `family_holdout.py`）：包括聚类划分和整家族留出，可复用于其他蛋白功能预测器的严格评估。
- **ESM-2 嵌入流水线**（`src/tardiscreen/embed.py`）：可独立使用，为自定义 IDP 模型提供特征提取。
- **License**：MIT，允许自由使用和修改，但需确认具体文件是否包含第三方代码。
readme:
# AnHydra

**Paste a protein sequence. Find out whether it looks like it can survive drying out.**

Live at **[anhydra.work](https://anhydra.work)** · built for **SwampHacks XII** (Oct 16–18, 2026, UF)

Tardigrades survive losing essentially all of their water. A handful of protein families do that
work — CAHS in tardigrades, LEA and dehydrins in plants — by turning the cell's interior into glass
instead of letting it crystallise. Finding more of them is a real screening problem for
biopreservation research: vaccines, clotting factors and reagents that could ship without a cold
chain. AnHydra scores any amino-acid sequence for that character and explains the score in plain
language.

> **Read this first.** AnHydra is a **family classifier and triage tool**, not an efficacy predictor.
> It answers *"does this sequence belong to the desiccation-protective families?"* — never *"how much
> does this protein protect?"* Every limitation we know of is listed in
> [docs/METHODS.md](docs/METHODS.md).

*(The repository and the Python package are named `tardiscreen`, the project's working title.
AnHydra is the same thing.)*

Release checks and deployment gates: [docs/RELEASE.md](docs/RELEASE.md).
The API accepts one sequence of **20–1,022 standard residues**, including an optional FASTA
header. Longer inputs are rejected instead of silently scoring only a prefix. Scores are
uncalibrated classifier outputs, not experimentally measured protection probabilities.
The results below are recorded experiments; they have not been regenerated with the release fixes.

---

## How it works

| 1 · Data | 2 · Embed | 3 · Model | 4 · Explain | 5 · App |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Protective IDPs vs. *other disordered* proteins, matched on disorder and length | ESM-2 protein language model → a 480-number vector per sequence | A classifier head on those vectors, plus a parallel interpretable biophysical model | Feature contributions + a Gemini plain-language readout | FastAPI on Vultr, real domain, HTTPS |

ESM-2 is **frozen** — we never touched Meta's 35M pretrained weights. What we trained is the thin
classifier sitting on top of them, which is called *linear probing*. The second, interpretable model
provides auxiliary signatures for the "why" panel; it does not replace ESM-2 if embedding fails.

## The question that makes this hard

"Is this protein disordered?" is trivial — composition alone nearly solves it. "Among disordered
proteins, which ones *protect*?" is the question a lab actually has. We report both, because the
contrast is a better result than either number alone.

## Results

ROC-AUC under 5-fold cross-validation **split by sequence cluster** (CD-HIT 40% identity), never by
row. Clusters stay within one partition, but related sequences can remain in different clusters;
this split does not eliminate all homology between training and test sets.

- **trivial** — protective vs. *ordered* folded proteins. A sanity check.
- **real** — protective vs. *other disordered* proteins, matched one-to-one on disorder coverage and
  length. The question the project exists to ask.

| model | what it uses | trivial | real |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| composition | 20 amino-acid frequencies | 0.922 | 0.897 |
| biophysical | 9 interpretable features | 0.893 | 0.780 |
| BLAST | classical alignment search | 0.977 | 0.981 |
| CNN | DeepFam-style, trained from scratch | 0.987 | 0.965 |
| **ESM-2** | **pretrained protein language model** | **0.998** | **0.990** |

### That table does not justify the ML approach — so we kept going

BLAST (0.981) and ESM-2 (0.990) are within about one standard deviation. A 1990s alignment search
nearly matches the language model. Stratifying held-out sequences by how much alignment signal they
had shows why:

| best bitscore to training set | n | % protective | BLAST | ESM-2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| none / very weak | 482 | 12% | 0.925 | 0.947 |
| weak | 290 | 78% | 1.000 | 0.999 |
| moderate | 219 | 85% | 1.000 | 1.000 |

Read the **% protective** column. *"Does this protein have a close relative in the training set?"* is
close to the entire classifier — the positives are a few dense families whose members stay related
through a 40% identity split, while the negatives are unrelated singletons.

So we removed that advantage: **hold out an entire family**, train on the rest, test on a family with
no members of that annotated family in training. Related families can remain.

| held-out family | n | BLAST | ESM-2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| LEA | 308 | 0.739 | **0.818** |
| dehydrin | 198 | 0.925 | **0.934** |
| **mean** | | **0.832** | **0.876** |

LEA is the cleaner test — dehydrins are LEA group 2, so holding them out still leaves relatives in
training, which is why BLAST manages 0.925 there. With the annotated LEA family held out, BLAST falls to
0.739 while the language model holds at 0.818.

**This is the finding.** BLAST and ESM-2 have similar measured AUC on the cluster-split benchmark.
ESM-2 has higher measured AUC on these two annotated family holdouts. The families are related,
and these experiments do not establish performance for arbitrary uncatalogued organisms.

## The CNN rediscovered a published motif on its own

The CNN is trained from scratch on raw sequence: no pretraining, no hand-designed features, no motif
database. Its convolution filters are pattern detectors, so after training we can ask what makes them
fire. Ranking filters by how well their activation separates the classes and reading the
strongest-activating windows produced 48 exported motifs (up to 12 per kernel width, above the
configured activation-AUC threshold). These rankings describe the fitted model, not independent
test-set performance:

| filter | AUC | learned pattern |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 81 | 0.914 | `FLDKIKEKL` |
| 22 | 0.896 | `IKEKLPGYH` |
| 59 | 0.893 | `EKKGIMDKI` |
| 26 | 0.893 | `EKIKEKLPG` |
| 102 | 0.886 | `KGIKEKIKE` |

Residue content across all learned motifs: **K 31%**, I 15%, E 12%, G 10%, D 7%, L 6%.

The dehydrin family is *defined* by a lysine-rich 15-residue motif, the
[K-segment](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4215689), consensus `EKKGIMDKIKEKLPG`. The
filters reconstruct it:

```
canonical K-segment   E K K G I M D K I K E K L P G
filter 59             E K K G I M D K I
filter 26                     E K I K E K L P G
filter 81                   F L D K I K E K L
```

Filter 59 matches the first nine residues exactly. Filter 26 covers the last nine with E where the
canonical has D — and the published consensus is `[XKXGXX(D/E)KIK(D/E)KXPG]`, which permits either at
that position ([Malik et al. 2017](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5415607/)). The 31%
lysine content matches the same literature's finding that lysines are the most conserved residues in
the segment.

**Nothing in the pipeline was told this motif exists.** A network with 101k parameters, trained on
1,049 sequences, recovered a motif that plant biologists named and published decades ago.

It is also the *right* motif for this dataset rather than the expected one. We predicted glycine and
serine repeats, the CAHS signature. The dataset contains **no CAHS proteins** — the 529 matched
positives comprise 308 LEA, 198 dehydrins, 21 other protective proteins and 2 hydrophilins — so the
network learned what is actually there. Had it produced what we expected, we would
have had more reason to suspect we were fooling ourselves.

This is the one result none of the other four models can produce. ESM-2 scores better; it cannot tell
you what it saw.

## We did not believe our own number

The real task first scored **0.987**, far above what we predicted. We treated that as a bug. Four
hypotheses, four tests: cross-validation leakage (a shuffled-label check sat at chance), length
(length-only AUC fell to 0.514 while ESM-2 held), source database (removed), and disorder
itself — **which turned out to be the real problem.** The original negatives were folded proteins
with a floppy tail, median disorder coverage 0.15 against 0.88 for the positives.

So we rebuilt the entire negative set from genuinely disordered UniProt proteins, matched one-to-one
on disorder coverage *and* length under the caliper from
[Austin (2011)](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3120982/). Both variables came out
balanced before downstream filtering (|SMD| ≤ 0.015, threshold 0.10). The committed final evaluation
contains 529 positives and 520 negatives; that initial balance check does not establish balance
after exclusions.

Every threshold, its published source, the full confound table and all nine limitations are in
**[docs/METHODS.md](docs/METHODS.md)**.

## Repo layout

```
anhydra/  (repo: tardiscreen)
├── app/
│   ├── main.py             FastAPI: sequence in → score + explanation out
│   └── static/index.html   built-in fallback results page
├── src/tardiscreen/
│   ├── data.py             pull + label UniProt / DisProt / MobiDB sequences
│   ├── build_negatives.py  candidate pool of genuinely disordered proteins
│   ├── coverage.py         per-sequence disorder coverage
│   ├── match_negatives.py  caliper matching on coverage + length
│   ├── merge_dataset.py    fold the matched negatives into the dataset
│   ├── features.py         9 interpretable biophysical features
│   ├── embed.py            ESM-2 embeddings
│   ├── model.py            classifier head + feature model → data/models.joblib
│   ├── evaluate.py         cluster-split CV, ROC/PR-AUC, confusion matrix
│   ├── blast_baseline.py   classical alignment baseline
│   ├── remote_homology.py  stratify test sequences by alignment signal
│   ├── family_holdout.py   leave-one-family-out generalization
│   ├── cnn.py              DeepFam-style CNN trained from scratch
│   ├── motifs.py           read motifs back out of the CNN's filters
│   ├── diagnose.py         the confound checks
│   └── explain.py          Gemini plain-language "why this score"
├── docs/
│   ├── METHODS.md          every threshold, its source, and all limitations
│   ├── DEMO.md             the presentation + live-demo script
│   ├── EXPLAINER.md        the whole project in plain English
│   └── results/            the CSVs and figures behind every number above
├── frontend/               React UIs; older variants remain for compatibility
│   └── anhydra-site/       current site: landing, screener, about, privacy
├── deploy/                 systemd unit + Caddy config for the Vultr host
└── scripts/check_site.sh   is the live site demo-ready?
```

## Quick start

Copy `.env.example` to `.env`. For local scoring without Auth0 or PostgreSQL, set
`APP_ENV=development` and `AUTH_DEV_ANONYMOUS=true` in that file and keep the server
bound to localhost. For production, follow [deployment setup](deploy/README.md)
and select matching frontend/backend authentication modes explicitly.

The commands below rebuild the data and model from scratch. An existing deployment
with compatible artifacts does not need retraining.

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt

python -m tardiscreen.data          # pull + label sequences
python -m tardiscreen.coverage      # disorder coverage
python -m tardiscreen.build_negatives
python -m tardiscreen.match_negatives
python -m tardiscreen.merge_dataset
python -m tardiscreen.embed         # ESM-2 embeddings (CPU is fine)
python -m tardiscreen.evaluate      # cluster-split CV
python -m tardiscreen.model         # writes data/models.joblib for the app

uvicorn app.main:app --env-file .env --host 127.0.0.1 --reload
```

Set `GEMINI_API_KEY` in `.env` for the plain-language readout. Without it the
app falls back to a local template rather than failing. Without `data/models.joblib`, `/score`
returns 503 rather than inventing a number.

For the current React site, follow [its README](frontend/anhydra-site/README.md).
To check the deployed site: `bash scripts/check_site.sh https://anhydra.work`.
Protected deployments require `AUTH_HEADER_FILE` as described in [backend operations](deploy/AUTH.md).

## Sponsor stack

- **Vultr** — hosts the app. No GPU needed; ESM-2 small embeds on CPU.
- **Gemini API** — writes the plain-language "why this score" readout.
- **GoDaddy Registry** — [anhydra.work](https://anhydra.work).
- **DEV** — the write-up.

Tracks: **Most Creative Use of AI**, **Overall**, **Easy on the Eyes**.

## References

- Lin et al., *Language models of protein sequences at the scale of evolution* — ESM-2.
- Seo et al. (2018), [DeepFam](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6022622/) — the CNN architecture.
- Malik et al. (2017), [dehydrin K-segment consensus](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5415607/).
- Hughes & Graether, [K-segment structure](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4215689/).
- Austin (2011), [caliper width for matching](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC3120982/).
- Rost (1999), [twilight zone of sequence alignment](https://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/teaching/statgen/2004/refs/rost1.pdf).

## 是什么

Skills-BIOKT 是一个由西班牙巴斯克大学 BioKT 实验室（理论生物化学实验室）开发和维护的 Claude Code skills 集合，用于分子模拟和计算生物化学。它提供了一系列可复用的技能（skills），涵盖 GROMACS/AMBER 分子动力学模拟的准备与安装、小分子参数化、DFT 计算、PLUMED 增强采样（伞形采样、元动力学、副本交换）以及 Bash 并行化等任务，旨在通过 AI 辅助自动化这些计算流程。

## 亮点

- **模块化技能设计**：每个技能独立封装为 SKILL.md 文件，便于按需调用和组合，降低了使用门槛。
- **覆盖完整模拟工作流**：从 GROMACS 安装（含 PLUMED、GPU、MPI 支持）到模拟准备（力场、溶剂化、平衡、生产、AWH、H-REMD、伞形采样），再到增强采样分析（WHAM、sum_hills、reweighting、block error analysis），形成闭环。
- **提供模板和参考文档**：包含 Slurm 作业脚本、WHAM 分析脚本、块自由能计算脚本等模板，以及 AWH、H-REMD、配体处理等参考文档，便于直接使用和修改。
- **AI 辅助并行化**：`bash-parallelize` 技能能识别任务中的独立工作项并利用子代理并行执行，同时检查系统负载，体现了智能化的任务调度。
- **实验室背景契合课题**：该实验室本身专注于无序蛋白和耦合折叠-结合研究，因此技能设计直接针对此类模拟需求。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接服务于 IDR/IDP 相关的分子模拟研究，其技能覆盖了无序蛋白模拟的关键环节：
- **GROMACS 模拟准备**（`gmx-prep`）支持 AWH、H-REMD 等增强采样方法，这些方法常用于采样无序蛋白的构象系综和折叠-结合过程。
- **PLUMED 增强采样技能**（`plumed-us`、`plumed-metad`、`plumed-remd`）提供了伞形采样、元动力学和副本交换的完整设置与分析流程，可用于计算自由能面、研究无序蛋白的相互作用和相分离行为。
- **小分子参数化**（`amber-parameterize`）和 **DFT 计算**（`dft-homo-lumo`）可用于研究蛋白-配体相互作用，包括无序蛋白与金属离子或其他分子的结合。
- **Bash 并行化**（`bash-parallelize`）可加速大规模构象采样或参数扫描，提高计算效率。

这些技能可以直接被 IDR/IDP 研究者采用，以自动化模拟流程，减少手动操作错误，并加速研究周期。

## 怎么用

- **安装**：克隆仓库并运行 `install.sh`，将技能符号链接到 `~/.claude/skills/`。
  ```bash
  git clone https://github.com/BioKT/Skills-BIOKT.git
  cd Skills-BIOKT
  bash install.sh
  ```
- **更新**：`git pull && bash install.sh`。
- **调用**：在 Claude Code 会话中通过斜杠命令调用，如 `/gmx-prep`、`/plumed-metad` 等。
- **依赖**：需要 Claude Code 环境；具体技能依赖 GROMACS、AMBER、PLUMED、PySCF 等外部软件，但仓库本身不包含这些依赖的安装（除 `gmx-install` 技能指导源码编译）。
- **输入/输出**：输入通常为 PDB 结构文件、力场参数、模拟参数等；输出为模拟轨迹、自由能文件、分析结果（如 WHAM 输出）。具体格式因技能而异，详见各 SKILL.md。
- **调试/示例**：仓库提供模板脚本（如 `slurm_gmx.sh`、`wham.py`）和参考文档，可作为起点；但未提供完整的示例数据集或单元测试。
- **GPU 需求**：`gmx-install` 支持 CUDA 编译，因此模拟可受益于 GPU 加速，但并非强制。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学洞察在于将复杂的分子模拟工作流（从安装、准备到增强采样分析）封装为 AI 可调用的技能，通过标准化和自动化降低使用门槛，同时利用实验室在无序蛋白模拟方面的经验，确保技能针对此类系统进行了优化。其价值在于“可复用的 AI 辅助模拟流程”，而非单一算法创新。

## 可搬移点

# Skills-BIOKT

Claude Code skills for molecular simulation and computational biochemistry, developed and maintained by the [BioKT lab](https://sites.google.com/view/biokt) (Theoretical Biochemistry Laboratory) at the University of the Basque Country (UPV/EHU) and the Donostia International Physics Center (DIPC).

## About the lab

The BioKT group works at the intersection of chemical physics and biochemistry, with a focus on protein dynamics, folding, and binding. Research topics include:

- Intrinsically disordered proteins and coupled folding-binding
- Protein conformational transitions studied with optical tweezers and AFM
- Kinetic models of metastable states using master equation approaches ([MasterMSM](https://github.com/daviddesancho/MasterMSM))
- Quantum mechanical investigations of protein–metal interactions

Simulations are run primarily with GROMACS and AMBER, analysed with MDtraj, and enhanced sampling is performed with PLUMED.

## Skills

| Skill | Description |
|---|---|
| `gmx-prep` | GROMACS MD simulation preparation: force field setup, solvation, equilibration, production, AWH, H-REMD, umbrella sampling |
| `gmx-install` | GROMACS source build with PLUMED, GPU (CUDA), and MPI support; includes benchmark testing |
| `amber-parameterize` | Small-molecule parameterization with AmberTools (antechamber, parmchk2, tleap); GAFF/GAFF2 force fields; GROMACS conversion via acpype |
| `dft-homo-lumo` | DFT geometry optimisation and HOMO/LUMO frontier orbital analysis using PySCF |
| `bash-parallelize` | Identify independent work items in a task description or bash loop and run them in parallel using subagents; safety-checks system load before launching |
| `plumed-us` | Umbrella sampling setup and analysis with PLUMED: multi-window RESTRAINT input files, WHAM analysis, free energy profiles and error bars |
| `plumed-metad` | Metadynamics setup and analysis with PLUMED: well-tempered metadynamics, free energy surfaces with sum_hills, reweighting, block error analysis, convergence assessment |
| `plumed-remd` | Replica simulations with PLUMED: umbrella sampling with replica exchange, bias-exchange metadynamics, parallel-tempering metadynamics, trajectory demuxing and WHAM analysis |

## Installation

Clone this repository and run `install.sh` to symlink all skills into `~/.claude/skills/`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/BioKT/Skills-BIOKT.git
cd Skills-BIOKT
bash install.sh
```

To update on any machine:

```bash
git pull && bash install.sh
```

## Usage

Invoke a skill from any Claude Code session:

```
/gmx-prep
/gmx-install
/gmx-install test
/amber-parameterize
/dft-homo-lumo
/bash-parallelize
/plumed-us
/plumed-metad
/plumed-remd
```

## 是什么

BioGraphX 是一个可解释的物理化学图编码框架，用于从序列出发预测蛋白质和 RNA 的功能属性（如亚细胞定位、无序性、溶解性）。它通过构建残基/核苷酸间的确定性相互作用图，将生物物理规则编码为特征，无需预测结构或序列比对。

## 亮点

- **无需结构或 MSA**：仅从序列构建图，避免了对预测结构的依赖，降低了计算成本。
- **可解释性**：每个特征都可追溯到具体的生物物理规则，便于理解模型决策。
- **跨域通用**：同一编码框架适用于蛋白质、RNA，覆盖定位、无序、溶解性等多个任务。
- **参数高效**：在溶解性任务中仅用 1.44M 参数达到与 6M 参数模型相当的性能，体现绿色 AI 理念。
- **性能领先**：在 DeepLoc 2.0 上达到 SOTA，miRNA 定位 AUROC 0.9396，无序预测 AUC 0.899。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接针对 IDR/IDP 预测（BioGraphX-IDP），其核心思想——用物理化学图编码替代结构预测——对无序蛋白研究极具价值。无序蛋白缺乏稳定结构，传统结构依赖方法受限，而该框架从序列出发，通过残基间相互作用能力编码，可捕捉无序区域的局部化学倾向。此外，其“物理 vs 进化”信号分解方法（通过混合权重扫描）为理解 IDR 预测中物理与进化信息的贡献提供了新视角，可迁移至构象系综或 LLPS 互作建模。

## 怎么用

- **入口**：仓库未提供可直接运行的代码或命令行工具，仅展示概念和结果。README 中提供了在线演示（https://abubakar-saeed.github.io），可粘贴序列实时构建图并查看特征。
- **依赖**：未列出具体依赖文件，但根据工具标签推测使用 Python、PyTorch、XGBoost、SHAP、ESM-2、RiNALMo、BioPython。
- **数据格式**：输入为蛋白质或 RNA 序列（FASTA 格式），输出为每个残基/核苷酸的特征向量及预测标签。
- **GPU**：需要 GPU 加速，尤其是使用 ESM-2 等大型语言模型时。
- **调试**：无单元测试或示例脚本，但可通过在线演示交互式探索。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学是“相互作用能力编码”：通过序列分离和残基化学性质确定边，构建确定性图，而非预测几何结构。这种表示与接触图互补，能捕捉序列局部的化学兼容性，从而在无需结构的情况下保留生物物理信号。其创新在于将物理规则显式编码为可解释特征，并通过门控机制与预训练语言模型（如 ESM-2）融合，实现物理与进化信息的可调平衡。

## 可搬移点

- **图编码模块**：将序列转换为残基/核苷酸相互作用图的逻辑，可独立解耦，用于自定义的 IDR 或互作预测 Pipeline。
- **特征门控机制**：在 IDP 任务中，用 61 个物理特征对 ESM-2 嵌入进行门控，该机制可迁移至其他无序蛋白预测模型。
- **物理-进化混合扫描**：通过调整物理与进化特征的权重，分析任务对两种信号的依赖，此方法可复用于研究 IDR 预测中的信号来源。
- **License**：README 未明确说明，需确认。
