# Droplet

Lattice Monte Carlo simulations of polymers and biomolecular condensates. The repo also
holds a continuum pipeline for condensate-mediated enhancer–promoter sensing:
single-sphere prewetting → two-sphere BVP → 1D first-passage solver → Rouse-chain
simulation → Fisher information. The Julia core is in `src/`. Experiments are spec files
under `spec/`, and figures are made in the three `viz*.ipynb` notebooks. `CLAUDE.md` and
`context/*.md` document the lattice-MC conventions.

## Setup

`Manifest.toml` was resolved with **Julia 1.11.1**, so use exactly that version. Install
it with [juliaup](https://github.com/JuliaLang/juliaup):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://install.julialang.org | sh    # installs juliaup; open a new shell afterwards
juliaup add 1.11.1
juliaup default 1.11.1                           # runJL calls plain `julia`, so the default must be 1.11.1
julia --version                                  # -> julia version 1.11.1
```

Pin `1.11.1` rather than relying on the `release` channel, because `juliaup update` moves
`release` to the newest version. To run a single command on 1.11.1 without changing the
default, use `julia +1.11.1 ...`.

Then install the Julia and Python dependencies:

```bash
julia --project=@. -e 'using Pkg; Pkg.instantiate()'
pip install -r requirements.txt jupyter        # numpy 2.2.6, scipy, matplotlib, numdifftools, pillow
```

- **Run everything from the repo root.** `--project=@.` finds `Project.toml` from the
  working directory, and every `data/...` path in specs, `param.jl` files and notebooks
  is relative to it.
- The figures use `text.usetex = True`, so a LaTeX install is needed.
- NumPy ≥ 2.4 removed `np.trapz`. In `viz-rouse.ipynb` only cell 12 and the legacy cells
  call it. Swap in `np.trapezoid` or use the pinned 2.2.6.
- `data/` and `spec/jobs/` (cluster copies of specs) are gitignored. On a fresh clone,
  regenerate the data as described below. `media/figures/` is tracked and holds the
  reference PDFs.

## Notebooks

| Notebook | Contents |
|---|---|
| `viz.ipynb` | Lattice-MC experiments from Nov 2025 to Aug 2026: 3D polymer and density maps, filament and enhancer prewetting, polymer and heteropolymer phases, looping, transcription and enhancer search, binding curves, Gillespie mRNA accumulation and LLR, polymer MSD, and Flory–Huggins phase diagrams. Reads `data/<date>/<exp>/output_cpu*.json` from `spec/*.jl` sweeps. |
| `viz-mc.ipynb` | MC proximal-promoter transcription analysis (`data/20260417`, `20260418`, `20260823`): ON/OFF times with hysteresis, conditional local concentration, Fisher rates with bootstrap errors, decision time. |
| `viz-rouse.ipynb` | The continuum/Rouse pipeline: two-sphere pair potentials, FPT PDFs, Rouse vs 1D Fisher information, Fisher rate vs concentration and vs genomic separation, prewetting constructions, and single-sphere Fisher rates. See [Reproducing viz-rouse.ipynb](#reproducing-viz-rouseipynb). |

## Running scripts

### Parallel sweeps: `runJL` + `sim/sweep.jl`

```bash
./runJL sim/sweep.jl <specfile> <ncpus> <outdir>
```

- `runJL` starts `ncpus` copies of `julia --project=@. sim/sweep.jl <specfile> <k> <ncpus> <outdir>`
  joined by pipes, so they all run at once. Only the last process's stdout reaches the
  terminal, but stderr from every process does. **Specs must not print to stdout.**
  Once a downstream process exits, an upstream one that prints dies with `EPIPE` and
  writes no output. Use `@info`/`@warn`, which go to stderr.
- `<specfile>` must be relative to the repo root, because `sweep.jl` does `include("../" * specfile)`
  from `sim/`. An absolute path breaks.
- The spec must define `slist, alphas, betas, nparams, blurb, checkpoint_path, target!`.
  CPU `k` runs `keya = (k-1)n+1 … kn` with `n = div(nparams, ncpus)`, and each of those
  runs every `beta`. **The remainder is silently dropped**, so pick an `ncpus` that
  divides `nparams`.
- Output is `<outdir>/output_cpu<k>.json`, shaped `{keya: {keyb: record}}`.
- Several `runJL` lines can be piped together to run concurrently; see `run.sh`.

### `spec/local/<date>/`: snapshots of what ran that day

- **Lattice-MC specs** (≤ 2026-03) are dated copies of `spec/*.jl` files, run as above.
  Their contract is in `context/spec_template_guide.md`.
- **Job folders** (≥ 2026-07-20), e.g. `spec/local/20260912/test3/`, contain a
  `param.jl` and verbatim copies of the stage scripts. `param.jl` defines `PARAMS`,
  the single source of truth. Every script does `include(joinpath(@__DIR__, "param.jl"))`,
  then reads its inputs from and writes its outputs to `PARAMS.sim.output_dir`.
  To change a run, edit `param.jl`, never the scripts. `spec/local/make_grid.jl`
  generates one folder per parameter-grid cell.

| Stage script (in a job folder) | How to run | Reads → writes (in `PARAMS.sim.output_dir`) |
|---|---|---|
| `demo_bvp.jl` (single sphere) | `julia --project=@. <folder>/demo_bvp.jl` | → `demo_bvp_profiles.json` |
| `fisher_two_spheres.jl` (two-sphere BVP, sharded over gap `d`) | `./runJL sim/sweep.jl <folder>/fisher_two_spheres.jl <n_d+1> <output_dir>` | → `output_cpu*.json`, `bridged_seed_*.json` |
| `bvp_potential_interp.jl` | `julia --project=@. <folder>/bvp_potential_interp.jl` | `output_cpu*.json` → `bvp_potential_interp.json` |
| `fisher_rate_from_fpt_solver.jl` | `julia --project=@. <folder>/fisher_rate_from_fpt_solver.jl` | `bvp_potential_interp.json` → `fisher_rate_from_fpt_solver.json` |
| `rouse_mfpt_attractive.jl` | `./runJL sim/sweep.jl <folder>/rouse_mfpt_attractive.jl <ncpus> <other_dir>` | both JSONs above → `<other_dir>/output_cpu*.json` |
| `sweep_rouse_s.jl` | `julia --project=@. <folder>/sweep_rouse_s.jl` | reruns interp + FPT for each `s` → `fisher_vs_rouse_s.json` |

For the sweep specs, `sim/sweep.jl` stamps `spec_path`, `output_dir` and `ncpus` into
`PARAMS.sim` *after* the include, so every record carries its own provenance under
`record["params"]["sim"]`.

### Example: `rouse_mfpt_attractive.jl`

```bash
./runJL sim/sweep.jl spec/local/20260912/test3/rouse_mfpt_attractive.jl 30 data/20260912/rouse
```

- **Inputs** are read at include time from the `output_dir` in `param.jl`
  (`data/20260912/test3`). Run `bvp_potential_interp.jl` and
  `fisher_rate_from_fpt_solver.jl` first.
- **The outdir must differ** from that `output_dir`. Otherwise it overwrites the BVP
  `output_cpu*.json`.
- **`alphas`** are the solver's φ∞ values (`n_phi − 2 = 30`), thinned to `n_phi_run`.
  The script warns if `ncpus` does not divide `nparams`.
- **Run-length knobs** live in the spec, not in `param.jl`: `nsteps`, `n_phi_run`,
  `save_mode` and `seed0`. Size `nsteps` against `tau_rouse`.
- **Seeds** are `seed0 + keya`, so the RNG stream does not depend on `ncpus`. Output is
  still not bit-reproducible across machines or BLAS kernels, so compare statistics,
  not bits.
- **Start small** (`nsteps = 1_000_000`, few CPUs), time it, then scale up.

## Reproducing viz-rouse.ipynb

### 1. Data

Skip any step whose output already exists. The steps marked ✓ were re-run on
2026-10-07 and matched the stored files bit for bit.

```bash

./runJL sim/sweep.jl spec/local/20260902/test3/fisher_two_spheres.jl 18 data/20260902/test3

# (b) Fan the BVP output out. The three downstream dirs hold byte-identical copies.
for d in data/20260912/test3 data/20260912/test3_clone data/20260927/s110; do
  mkdir -p $d && cp data/20260902/test3/output_cpu*.json $d/; done

# (c) Main chain (s = 300, a = 20, R = 130): interp + FPT take ~1.5 min.   ✓
julia --project=@. spec/local/20260912/test3/bvp_potential_interp.jl
julia --project=@. spec/local/20260912/test3/fisher_rate_from_fpt_solver.jl
julia --project=@. spec/local/20260912/test3/demo_bvp.jl
julia --project=@. spec/local/20260902/test3/demo_bvp.jl      # only the binodal is read

# (d) Rouse chain: the expensive step. First edit spec/local/20260912/test3/rouse_mfpt_attractive.jl

./runJL sim/sweep.jl spec/local/20260912/test3/rouse_mfpt_attractive.jl 30 data/20260912/rouse

# (e) Fisher vs genomic separation (s = 5…1000, 64 values; budget ≲1.5 h).

for r in small_R medium_R large_R; do julia --project=@. spec/local/20261004/$r/demo_bvp.jl; done

```

**Folder-name pitfall in step (g).** The notebook needs `data/20260825/run1…run5` to hold

those values. After the loop, rotate the output folders:

```bash
python -c "import json;[print(r,json.load(open(f'data/20260825/{r}/demo_bvp_profiles.json'))['params']['surface']['omega_b']) for r in ['run1','run2','run3','run4','run5']]"
```

**BVP seeding in step (a).** `bvp.seed_path` warm-starts the bridged branch from

with a warning and writes new seeds. Rerunning into the same directory then
warm-starts every gap. This path has not been re-run, so it is not verified to reproduce

one_liner: PhaseLACE 是一个基于蛋白语言模型和构象表征的 LLPS 相关蛋白预测工具，虽聚焦相分离而非直接建模无序蛋白分子互作机制，但其序列-构象联合建模思路对 IDP/IDR 互作预测有可迁移价值。

## 是什么
PhaseLACE 是一个面向生物分子凝聚体研究的蛋白序列预测模型，用于识别液–液相分离（LLPS）相关蛋白，并提供序列内部的局部预测证据。它结合预训练的序列与构象相关表征、可学习的邻域模式和全蛋白上下文，通过多成员共识输出蛋白级预测。

## 亮点
- **联合表征**：同时利用蛋白语言模型（ESM2-8M）的序列信息和构象预测模型（ALBATROSS）的隐藏表示，形成 650 维逐残基特征。
- **局部–全局建模**：用可学习的残基邻域特征（深度可分离卷积）结合全序列上下文，形成位置相关的判别证据。
- **多尺度共识**：在三个序列窗口（33、129、257 aa）上整合证据，再对三个独立训练成员的蛋白概率取平均，提升鲁棒性。
- **轻量高效**：每个成员仅 42,377 个可训练参数，下游预测器共 55,508 个参数，训练和推理开销低。
- **模块化设计**：代码文件清晰分离模型、训练、推理、评价，支持阶段式训练（先训练证据分支，再训练残差分支）。

## 为何对本课题有用
PhaseLACE 直接针对 IDR/IDP 与 LLPS 的互作预测问题，是课题方向的同向工具。其核心价值在于：
- **IDR 识别**：局部分数可定位无序区、低复杂度区等候选功能片段，为 IDR 功能研究提供证据。
- **LLPS 互作建模**：蛋白级分数支持候选序列排序，可用于筛选相分离相关蛋白，辅助互作网络分析。
- **方法可迁移**：其“序列–构象联合表征 + 局部–全局残差 + 多成员共识”的框架可迁移到其他无序蛋白预测任务（如结合位点预测、构象系综特性预测）。
- **计算效率**：轻量参数设计适合大规模蛋白组筛选，可集成到 IDP 构象采样或语言模型流水线中作为快速预筛模块。

## 怎么用
- **主入口**：`predict.py` 用于推理，`train.py` 用于训练，`evaluate.py` 和 `evaluate_regions.py` 用于评价。
- **安装**：Python 3.10+，运行 `python -m pip install -r requirements.txt`（依赖：numpy, torch, scikit-learn, scipy, safetensors）。
- **推理示例**：准备 `embeddings/protein.npy`（float32 的 [L,650] 矩阵）和三个成员权重，运行：
  ```bash
  python predict.py --features embeddings/protein.npy --checkpoints member1.pt member2.pt member3.pt --output prediction.json
  ```
  输出 JSON 包含蛋白级概率、成员概率和 33 aa 局部分数均值。
- **训练**：准备 CSV（含 feature_file, accession, label, category, sequence_sha256 等字段），运行 `prepare_data.py` 生成缓存，然后分阶段训练：
  ```bash
  python prepare_data.py --table metadata.csv --features-dir embeddings --output cache
  python train.py --stage baseline --cache cache/pooled --output runs/base --device cuda:0
  python train.py --stage phaselace --cache cache/raw --baseline-root runs/base --output runs/phaselace --device cuda:0
  ```
- **数据格式**：输入为 NPY 特征矩阵，输出为 JSON；训练数据为 CSV。
- **GPU 需求**：训练需要 GPU（`--device cuda:0`），推理也可在 CPU 上运行（但速度较慢）。
- **调试**：代码文件较少，可直接在 `model.py` 中设置断点；`predict.py` 提供了完整推理流程，适合作为调试入口。

## 核心 idea
PhaseLACE 的核心方法学在于“局部–全局残差增强”：先训练一个多尺度位置证据分支（基于序列–构象联合表征），然后固定该分支，用深度可分离卷积学习局部邻域模式，并结合全局上下文生成残差（系数 0.3）修正位置分数。这种“先学粗证据，再学细残差”的两阶段策略，使得模型在保持轻量参数的同时，能捕捉 IDR 中短程和长程的序列模式，并通过多成员共识提升泛化性。

## 可搬移点
- **特征融合模块**：`model.py` 中拼接 ESM2-8M 和 ALBATROSS 表征形成 650 维输入的逻辑，可直接复用于其他 IDP 预测任务（如结合位点、构象特性预测）。
- **多尺度位置证据分支**：33/129/257 aa 窗口的边界校正均值汇聚 + 共享 MLP 网络，可独立提取用于 IDR 区域打分。
- **局部–全局残差模块**：深度可分离卷积 + 全局池化 + 残差连接的设计，可迁移到其他序列预测模型，用于增强局部模式捕捉。
- **多成员共识机制**：三个独立训练成员的等权平均，可移植到任何分类器集成场景，提升稳定性。
- **许可证**：MIT 许可，允许自由使用和修改，但需保留上游署名（见 LICENSE）。

注意：以上可搬移点基于 README 描述，具体实现细节需查看源码确认；许可证为 MIT，允许商用和修改，但需确认上游依赖（如 ESM、ALBATROSS）的许可条款。
readme:
# PhaseLACE

**Local–global Augmentation with Consensus Ensembling**

PhaseLACE 是面向生物分子凝聚体研究的蛋白序列预测模型，用于识别液–液相分离（liquid–liquid phase separation，LLPS）相关蛋白，并提供序列内部的局部预测证据。它将预训练的序列与构象相关表征、可学习的邻域模式和全蛋白上下文结合起来，通过多成员共识输出蛋白级预测。

PhaseLACE 关注两个相互联系的问题：**哪些蛋白值得优先开展相分离实验，以及蛋白内部哪些片段值得进一步研究。** 蛋白级分数支持候选序列排序，局部分数支持无序区、低复杂度区及其他候选功能片段的分析。

- **联合表征：**同时利用蛋白语言模型提供的序列信息和构象预测模型提供的隐藏表示。
- **局部–全局建模：**用可学习的残基邻域特征结合全序列上下文，形成位置相关的判别证据。
- **多尺度共识：**在三个序列窗口上整合证据，再对三个独立训练成员的蛋白概率取平均。

本仓库提供模型定义、数据准备、训练、推理和评价源码。运行所需的数据、特征矩阵和权重由使用者单独提供；训练入口会生成可供推理的权重文件。

## 模型如何工作

PhaseLACE 从蛋白序列提取固定的逐残基表示，再训练下游预测器。整体流程如下：

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S["蛋白序列"] --> E["序列表征"]
    S --> A["构象相关表征"]
    E --> J["逐残基联合表示"]
    A --> J
    J --> M["多尺度位置证据"]
    E --> L["局部邻域与全局上下文"]
    M --> F["位置证据融合"]
    L --> F
    F --> P["成员蛋白概率"]
    P --> C["三成员共识预测"]
```

**序列–构象编码。** ESM2-8M提供每个残基的320维序列表征；ALBATROSS的三个构象预测网络分别提供110维隐藏表示，组合为330维构象相关表征。拼接后的输入为 `[L,650]`，其中 `L` 是蛋白长度。

**多尺度位置证据。** 模型使用33、129、257 aa三个窗口进行边界校正的均值汇聚，并由共享的650→20→5→1网络产生位置分数。该分支首先训练，在后续残差学习阶段固定。

**局部–全局残差。** 局部分支将序列表征投影为64维，通过两层深度可分离卷积学习邻域模式；全局分支将全序列表示汇聚为32维上下文。两者在各尺度、各位置拼接，经96→20→1网络生成残差，以0.3的系数修正位置分数。残差输出层零初始化，使训练从已学习的多尺度证据出发。

**共识读出。** 每个成员在各尺度取位置最大值、转换为概率后平均；PhaseLACE再对三个成员的蛋白概率取等权平均。每个成员有42,377个可训练残差参数，下游预测器共55,508个参数。

扩展版本 **PhaseLACE-Fusion** 将三个增强成员与三个跨内层划分训练的多尺度证据成员等权融合。它与PhaseLACE共享模型组件，以六成员共识输出最终概率。

## 主要结果

蛋白级评价包含17,643条非人蛋白，其中375条LLPS相关正例、17,268条背景蛋白。正例合并自组装型与伙伴依赖型蛋白，形成统一的蛋白级判别任务。

| 模型 | AUROC | 完整背景AUPR | AP | 平衡抽样AUPR |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| PhaseLACE（三成员） | **0.834791** | 0.162194 | 0.168105 | 0.838702 |
| PhaseLACE-Fusion（六成员） | **0.837802** | 0.175487 | 0.181172 | 0.843276 |

在匹配三个成员、模型种子与数据划分的比较中，PhaseLACE相对多尺度基础预测器的AUROC提高**1.47个百分点**，平衡抽样AUPR提高**1.06个百分点**。

表中结果先在每个外层折内计算，再取五折均值。AUPR为PR曲线梯形积分，AP为average precision；平衡抽样与完整背景使用不同类别比例，分别报告。局部分数用于候选片段分析，区域评价有独立的标注和汇总流程。

## 安装

Python 3.10及以上：

```bash
python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
```

本实现的推理入口接收已经提取的逐残基特征矩阵。[数据与编码资源](#数据与编码资源)提供从序列生成NPY文件的示例。

## 预测一个蛋白

准备 `embeddings/protein.npy` 和同一外层折的三个成员权重，然后运行：

```bash
python predict.py --features embeddings/protein.npy \
  --checkpoints member1.pt member2.pt member3.pt --output prediction.json
```

输入矩阵为float32的 `[L,650]`，通道次序为：ESM2-8M第6层320维，随后是ALBATROSS的asphericity、scaled radius of gyration、scaled end-to-end distance隐藏表示各110维。

输出JSON包含蛋白级预测分数 `probability`、各成员分数 `member_probabilities`、与序列等长的33 aa局部分数均值 `residue_33aa_mean`。权重支持训练脚本导出的 `inference.pt` 或兼容的外部 `safetensors` 文件。

使用Fusion时，另传 `--baseline-checkpoints base1.pt base2.pt base3.pt`。这三个权重来自同一外层折、不同内层划分的多尺度证据模型。局部分数均值用于描述性分析；论文区域结果按单成员和指定折汇总协议评价。

## 数据准备与训练

准备包含以下字段的CSV：

| 字段 | 含义 |
|---|---|
| `feature_file` | 相对于特征目录的NPY文件路径 |
| `accession` | 蛋白标识 |
| `label` | 0/1背景或LLPS相关蛋白标签 |
| `category` | 原数据来源类别，用于内层分层 |
| `sequence_sha256` | 输入氨基酸序列的SHA-256 |
| `fold`、`original_row` | 可选的固定外层折与原始行标识 |

未提供 `fold` 时，采用 `KFold(5, shuffle=True, random_state=711016)`。复现上述结果时，应使用相同的数据成员、类别和外层划分。

```bash
python prepare_data.py --table metadata.csv --features-dir embeddings --output cache

# 阶段一：训练多尺度位置证据分支
python train.py --stage baseline --cache cache/pooled --output runs/base --device cuda:0

# 阶段二：固定证据分支，训练局部–全局残差成员
python train.py --stage phaselace --cache cache/raw --baseline-root runs/base \
  --output runs/phaselace --device cuda:0
```

默认使用模型种子711016、711017、711018，内层划分种子20260904和五个外层折。训练采用Adam，初始学习率0.003、最多80轮；内层训练按1:1循环采样背景，完整覆盖背景后按内层AP选模，patience=8、min_delta=0.002。恢复时在同一命令后添加 `--resume`。

每个训练任务输出 `best.pt`、`last.pt` 和用于推理的纯张量 `inference.pt`。准备缓存前会检查磁盘空间，训练期间保存状态和恢复信息。

训练Fusion的额外成员时，固定模型种子711016，分别使用内层种子20260916、20260917、20260918和独立输出目录。例如：

```bash
python train.py --stage baseline --cache cache/pooled --seeds 711016 \
  --inner-seed 20260916 --output runs/inner20260916 --device cuda:0
```

## 评价

```bash
python evaluate.py --predictions "runs/phaselace/*/outer_predictions.csv" \
  --members 3 --output metrics.json
```

脚本展开通配符，校验成员的样本身份和覆盖，平均成员概率后计算各折指标。输入CSV需含 `row,label,probability,fold`；没有fold列时，提供 `--index cache/raw/train_index.csv`。Fusion传入三组增强成员和三组跨内层划分证据成员的预测，设 `--members 6`。

评价报告AUROC、AUPR、AP、Brier，以及100次平衡抽样的折均值。每次每类无放回抽取少数类样本数的80%，种子为2026091600+fold。模型选择使用内层AP，外层预测用于最终评价。

局部区域评价：

```bash
python evaluate_regions.py --scores local_scores.npy --annotations intervals.json \
  --coordinate-mode author --output region_metrics.json
```

`local_scores.npy`为一维33 aa局部概率；注释为1-based闭区间列表，如 `[[10,30],[70,90]]`。`author`兼容既有评价代码的 `mask[start:end]`，`standard`采用 `mask[start-1:end]`作坐标敏感性分析。两种结果分别报告；未注释位置作为注释比较背景。

## 代码文件

| 文件 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| `model.py` | PhaseLACE模型组件与前向计算 |
| `train.py`、`protocol.py`、`utils.py` | 训练流程、划分、采样、状态与恢复 |
| `prepare_data.py` | 特征矩阵与训练缓存准备 |
| `predict.py` | 三成员或Fusion推理 |
| `evaluate.py`、`evaluate_regions.py` | 蛋白与局部区域评价 |

## 数据与编码资源

序列编码使用 [ESM](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm)，构象相关编码使用 [ALBATROSS / Sparrow](https://github.com/idptools/sparrow)。本研究使用的联合特征提取方式与蛋白级数据视图沿用 [PSTP论文代码仓库](https://github.com/Morvan98/paper_code_PSTP)；其原始输入和缓存用于上述固定数据评价。

先按[特征提取软件的安装说明](https://github.com/Morvan98/PSTP#python-requirements)准备编码器兼容环境，再从氨基酸序列生成矩阵。该环境可与本仓库的训练环境分开，生成的NPY文件用于后续数据准备或推理。

```python
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from pstp.pstp_collections import pstp_embedding_by_batch

# 示例序列用于演示文件生成；实际使用时替换为待研究蛋白。
sequences = ["ACDEFGHIKLMNPQRSTVWY"]
matrices = pstp_embedding_by_batch(sequences)
Path("embeddings").mkdir(exist_ok=True)
np.save("embeddings/protein.npy", np.asarray(matrices[0], dtype=np.float32))
```

局部区域注释来源为 [PhaSePro](https://phasepro.elte.hu/)。请保留输入序列、构建体边界和坐标约定，以对应蛋白级与区域级评价。

## 许可与引用

MIT许可及上游署名见 `LICENSE`。PhaseLACE的多尺度证据路径沿用PSTP的读出定义；本模型的局部–全局残差路径和多成员共识在这一联合表征基础上完成LLPS判别。外部数据与编码器依其原始条款获取。

- 序列–构象相分离预测基础：Feng et al., *Briefings in Bioinformatics* (2025), [10.1093/bib/bbaf171](https://doi.org/10.1093/bib/bbaf171).
- 蛋白语言模型：Lin et al., *Science* (2023), [10.1126/science.ade2574](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.ade2574).
- 构象预测模型：Lotthammer et al., *Nature Methods* (2024), [10.1038/s41592-023-02159-5](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-023-02159-5).
- 区域注释：Mészáros et al., *Nucleic Acids Research* (2020), [10.1093/nar/gkz848](https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkz848).

## 是什么
ConformEval 是一个用于评估蛋白质语言模型（PLM）表征质量的基准测试工具包，通过三个任务（蛋白打结检测、折叠转换排序、残基无序性预测）来评估模型对蛋白质构象和固有无序区域（IDR）的编码能力。它提供数据、特征提取、下游预测器训练和评分工具，支持 ESM-2 和 ProtT5 等模型。

## 亮点
- **多任务基准设计**：涵盖三个互补的物理推断任务，每个任务有明确的输入、样本量和评估指标（AUROC、平均正样本排名百分位、平均精度）。
- **模块化架构**：清晰分离数据读取、特征提取、训练和评分，便于扩展新模型或任务。
- **灵活的模型适配**：通过配置文件（JSON）定义模型参数，支持 CPU 推理（默认 float32），并提供外部特征归档接口，允许集成任意编码器。
- **严格评估协议**：包含交叉验证、置信区间计算、数据泄漏检查（如样本身份、坐标、标签掩码），确保结果可靠性。
- **可复现性**：提供 Colab 教程、示例数据和命令行工具，降低使用门槛。

## 为何对本课题有用
该仓库直接针对 IDR/IDP 研究中的关键问题：评估 PLM 是否编码了与构象和紊乱相关的物理信息。其无序性预测任务（基于 DisProt 和 PDB 实验标签）为 IDR 预测提供标准基准，而打结和折叠转换任务则测试模型对全局构象和构象切换的敏感性。对于本课题，它提供了一个现成的评估框架，可用于：
- 比较不同 PLM（如 ESM-2、ProtT5）在 IDR 相关任务上的表现，指导模型选择。
- 通过特征提取和下游预测器训练，探索模型层与无序性预测的关系，助力理解模型内部表征。
- 作为基准，验证新的 IDR 预测方法或构象系综采样方法。

## 怎么用
- **安装**：`git clone https://github.com/wyqmath/ConformEval && cd ConformEval && python -m pip install .`（依赖见 `pyproject.toml`，核心依赖为 numpy、scipy、scikit-learn；可选依赖 `[esm2]` 或 `[prott5]` 需安装 torch 和 transformers）。
- **快速开始**：运行 `conformeval-evaluate --example --output-dir runs/knot-example`，输出评分到 `runs/knot-example/metrics.json`。
- **数据**：从 Zenodo 下载 `ConformEval-data.zip`（3.85 MB），解压到 `datasets/`，包含三个任务的 FASTA、TSV 标签文件和测试/验证划分。
- **特征提取**：使用 `conformeval-extract` 命令（需模型依赖），或参考 `examples/representation_archive.py` 生成外部特征（NPZ 文件 + JSON 索引）。
- **训练与评分**：`conformeval-prepare-inputs` 准备输入，`conformeval-fit-readers` 训练预测器，`conformeval-evaluate` 和 `conformeval-evaluate-residues` 分别评分序列级和残基级任务。
- **调试**：使用 Colab 教程（`examples/notebooks/ConformEval_tutorial.ipynb`）和示例数据（`examples/`）进行断点调试。
- **GPU 需求**：默认 CPU 推理，但 ESM-2 650M 等大模型建议 GPU 加速（需自行配置）。

## 核心 idea
核心方法学在于通过精心设计的基准任务和严格的评估协议，将 PLM 表征的“物理相关性”转化为可量化的指标，从而系统性地检验模型是否捕捉了蛋白质构象和紊乱的生物学特性。其创新点在于任务选择（打结、折叠转换、无序）覆盖了从局部到全局的构象特征，且通过交叉验证和置信区间确保评估的统计可靠性，为模型比较提供了公平的舞台。

## 可搬移点
- **评估协议**：`src/evaluate_predictions.py` 和 `src/evaluate_residue_predictions.py` 中的评分逻辑（AUROC、平均精度、置信区间）可直接复用，用于自定义 IDR 预测模型的评估。
- **特征提取接口**：`src/extract.py` 和 `src/model_interface.py` 中的模型适配层，可解耦后用于集成新的 PLM 或自定义特征提取器。
- **数据读取器**：`src/readers.py` 和 `src/datasets.py` 中的 FASTA/TSV 解析逻辑，可移植到其他蛋白质数据处理流程。
- **训练流程**：`src/train.py` 中的预测器训练和交叉验证逻辑，可调整后用于其他下游任务。
- **许可证**：MIT 许可证，允许自由使用和修改，但需注意数据集的单独许可条款（见 `sources.tsv`）。

# ConformEval: Protein Conformation Evaluation Benchmark

Protein function depends on the structures a sequence can adopt and the behavior of regions that remain disordered. Understanding how protein language models encode these properties helps assess their usefulness for studying the physical behavior of proteins. ConformEval (Protein Conformation Evaluation Benchmark) evaluates model representations through three tasks: protein knot detection, fold-switch ranking, and residue-level disorder prediction. It combines curated sequences and reference annotations with tools for extracting representations, training downstream predictors, and computing task-specific scores. The datasets comprise 734 knot samples, 8,879 fold-switch ranking items, and 1,279 disorder records. Adapters for [ESM-2](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm) and [ProtT5](https://github.com/agemagician/ProtTrans) and runnable examples let researchers evaluate their own models and examine how model layers and downstream predictors affect performance.

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23433394.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23433394)

[![Open in Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/wyqmath/ConformEval/blob/main/examples/notebooks/ConformEval_tutorial.ipynb)

## Quick start

Use Python 3.9 or later to run the scoring example:

```bash
git clone -c core.autocrlf=false https://github.com/wyqmath/ConformEval.git
cd ConformEval
python -m pip install .
conformeval-evaluate --example --output-dir runs/knot-example
```

The score is written to `runs/knot-example/metrics.json`. The [ConformEval tutorial](examples/notebooks/ConformEval_tutorial.ipynb) covers data download, representation extraction, predictor training, and scoring, using [ESM-2 8M](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm) as an example model.

## Tasks

| Task | Input | Samples | Metric |
|---|---|---:|---|
| Knot presence | Protein sequence | 734 | AUROC ↑ |
| Fold-switch ranking | Sequences of confirmed cases and background items | 8,879 | Mean positive rank percentile ↓ |
| Residue disorder | Protein sequence and residue labels | 1,279 records | Mean protein AP ↑ |

Knot presence includes 112 knotted and 622 unknotted samples. Fold-switch ranking includes 10 confirmed cases and 8,869 unlabeled background items. Disorder includes 391,718 labeled residues: 73,766 experimental disorder labels, 35 direct ordered labels, and 317,917 positions observed in experimental PDB structures. Unknown positions remain masked.

## Models

| Model | Configuration | Dimensions | Small three-task example | Full benchmark |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| [ESM-2 8M](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm) | [esm2_8m.json](configs/models/esm2_8m.json) | 320 | Tested | All three tasks |
| [ESM-2 650M](https://github.com/facebookresearch/esm) | [esm2_650m.json](configs/models/esm2_650m.json) | 1,280 | Tested | Refitting with the new adapter: Not tested |
| [ProtT5 XL encoder](https://github.com/agemagician/ProtTrans) | [prott5.json](configs/models/prott5.json) | 1,024 | Tested | Not tested |

Install the inference dependencies for your model:

```bash
python -m pip install '.[esm2]'
# For ProtT5:
python -m pip install '.[prott5]'
```

Model configurations select the checkpoint revision, layers, pooling, precision, and sequence window settings. Inference uses CPU float32 by default. The default window contains up to 1,022 residues with a 128-residue overlap. Overlapping residue vectors are averaged at their sequence coordinates before pooling; special and padding tokens are excluded. Set `long_sequence.policy` to `reject` to reject sequences longer than the configured window.

For another encoder, follow [representation_archive.py](examples/representation_archive.py) to supply an external feature archive. Each archive contains one NPZ file per sequence and a JSON index recording sequence IDs, lengths, model revision, layers, dimensions, pooling, extraction settings, and filenames. Residue vectors use one-based sequence coordinates. Predictor candidates and regularization values are configured in [training.json](configs/training.json).

## Data

[Download ConformEval-data.zip](https://zenodo.org/records/23433394/files/ConformEval-data.zip?download=1) (3.85 MB) from [Zenodo](https://zenodo.org/records/23433394).

```bash
curl --fail --location 'https://zenodo.org/records/23433394/files/ConformEval-data.zip?download=1' --output ConformEval-data.zip
unzip -q ConformEval-data.zip -d datasets
```

The archive extracts into `datasets/ConformEval-data/` with `knot_presence/`, `fold_switching/`, and `disorder/` directories. Each task includes `sequences.fasta`, `samples.tsv`, `test_splits.tsv`, and `validation_splits.tsv`; disorder also includes `labels.tsv`. The source register is `sources.tsv`.

The evaluator reads these task directories directly. Pass a task directory to `--data-dir` for input preparation and training, or the `ConformEval-data` directory to score both sequence-level tasks. Disorder scoring uses `--task-dir datasets/ConformEval-data/disorder`.

Tables use tab-separated UTF-8 text. Residue coordinates are one-based positions in the declared sequence. The [example inputs](examples/) use the same table formats, with one shared FASTA file for their synthetic sequences. Their sample tables mark `data_kind` as `synthetic` and require `--example`. Benchmark tables omit this column or use `benchmark`.

## Evaluation

Knot detection uses AUROC over chain-level predictions. Fold-switch ranking measures each held-out confirmed case's rank percentile within its test pool; the background is unlabeled and has no verified negative labels. Disorder scores known reference positions, calculates average precision for each protein record, and averages across records. The reported SD describes AP across the evaluated records and uses `ddof=0`.

All models use the same group assignments and scoring implementation. Knot and disorder tasks have five outer folds; fold-switch ranking has ten. Each outer training set has three inner validation folds for choosing model layers and predictor settings. Preprocessing is fitted on training data. Predictions are scored on outer test groups. The scoring commands accept TSV prediction files; [predictions/](examples/predictions/) contains example files and model metadata.

The scorers check sample identities, prediction coverage, folds, coordinates, and label masks. Confidence intervals resample groups from the saved predictions and exclude uncertainty from model refitting or dataset selection. The current splits support retrospective grouped-development evaluation. Complete biological-family independence has not been established; the source group audit has 37 unresolved PDB-key gaps.

## Repository layout

```text
ConformEval/
├── README.md
├── LICENSE
├── pyproject.toml
├── src/
├── configs/
│   ├── models/
│   │   ├── esm2_8m.json
│   │   ├── esm2_650m.json
│   │   └── prott5.json
│   ├── training.json
│   └── scoring.json
└── examples/
    ├── sequences.fasta
    ├── knot_presence/
    ├── fold_switching/
    ├── disorder/
    ├── predictions/
    ├── representation_archive.py
    └── notebooks/
        └── ConformEval_tutorial.ipynb
```

The examples contain 30 synthetic sequences, 20 knot samples, 20 ranking items, and 554 labeled residue positions. Their scores demonstrate the software interface. The [external-model example](examples/representation_archive.py) generates NumPy features in the format accepted by the trainer.

## Sources and license

Sequences and annotations come from [UniProt](https://www.uniprot.org/), [DisProt](https://disprot.org/), [RCSB PDB/SIFTS](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/pdbe/docs/sifts/), and KnotProt-derived annotations. Fold-switch cases follow [Porter and Looger (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1800168115). The downloaded dataset's `sources.tsv` records references, source versions, and reuse terms. KnotProt redistribution terms and the original scored-label source snapshot remain unresolved.

[MIT](LICENSE) covers the software. Source-specific data reuse terms are recorded in `ConformEval-data/sources.tsv` inside the [dataset ZIP](https://zenodo.org/records/23433394/files/ConformEval-data.zip?download=1).

## 是什么

这是一个基于 **Nextflow DSL2** 的自动化流水线，用于大规模蛋白质结构预测、固有无序性分析以及基因组注释质量评估。它整合了 **Protenix**（结构预测）、**Metapredict**（无序性预测）、**PSAURON**（编码序列质量评估）和 **InterProScan**（功能结构域注释）四个工具，并针对 HPC 环境（支持 SLURM）和 GPU 加速进行了优化。

## 亮点

- **模块化与可扩展性**：采用 Nextflow DSL2 设计，四个分析分支（Protenix、Metapredict、PSAURON、InterProScan）可独立开关，便于定制和扩展。
- **HPC 友好**：支持 SLURM 调度，通过分块（chunking）实现大规模并行，尤其针对计算密集的 Protenix 和 InterProScan。
- **智能分块策略**：使用贪心最长处理时间优先（LPT）装箱算法（`bin/balance_chunks.sh`）对序列进行长度均衡分块，避免因个别超大基因导致的计算倾斜。
- **统一输出与比较**：生成综合 PDF 报告和单行 TSV 摘要，便于跨物种比较和下游聚合分析。
- **轻量级容器化**：提供基于 Alpine 的轻量级基础容器，以及针对各工具的专用容器（如 Protenix、Metapredict、PSAURON），降低部署复杂度。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接针对 **IDR/IDP × 分子互作 × 计算与 AI** 课题，提供了以下关键价值：

- **固有无序性分析**：集成 Metapredict，可对蛋白质组进行高通量无序性预测，生成每个蛋白的无序性指标，并与多物种参考数据集比较，有助于研究 IDR 在相分离和分子识别中的作用。
- **结构预测与无序性结合**：通过 Protenix 预测结构，提取 pLDDT 分数，可区分有序与无序区域，为 IDR 构象系综研究提供结构基础。
- **注释质量评估**：PSAURON 和 InterProScan 的集成有助于识别错误注释的编码序列，确保 IDR 相关分析基于高质量数据。
- **可迁移的并行化思路**：其分块和并行化策略可迁移到其他大规模 IDR 分析流水线，如构象系综采样或无序蛋白语言模型推理。

## 怎么用

**安装与依赖**：
- 需要 Nextflow ≥ 23、Java 8+、Python 3.10，以及可选的 CUDA GPU。
- 使用 Singularity/Apptainer 容器，可通过 `bin/download_containers.sh` 下载预构建镜像，或通过 `nox -s build_apptainer` 本地构建。

**运行命令**：
```bash
nextflow run main.nf -profile singularity_slurm --fasta example.fasta --chunk_size 100
```
- 可选参数：`--run_protenix`、`--run_metapredict`、`--run_psauron`、`--run_interpro`（默认 false），以及 `--chunk_size`、`--ipr_chunks`、`--ipr_reference_json` 等。
- 输入为 FASTA 文件，输出存储在 `results/` 目录下，包括 PDF 报告、PNG 图、PKL 文件、CSV 和 TSV 文件。

**测试**：
- 提供单元测试 `tests/test_balance_chunks.py`，可运行 `pytest` 验证分块逻辑。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学在于**通过多维度指标（结构置信度、无序性、编码序列质量、功能域覆盖）综合评估基因组注释质量**，并利用**智能分块和并行化**实现蛋白质组规模的高通量分析。其创新点在于将多个独立工具无缝集成到一个可扩展的流水线中，并通过统一的比较和摘要机制，使研究者能够快速定位注释中的潜在问题区域。

## 可搬移点

- **分块算法**（`bin/balance_chunks.sh`）：贪心 LPT 装箱逻辑可独立提取，用于任何需要长度均衡分块的场景（如大规模序列分析）。
- **pLDDT 提取与绘图**（`bin/process_models.py`、`bin/plot_plddt.py`）：可复用其从 Protenix 输出中提取 pLDDT 并生成分布图的逻辑，用于 IDR 构象系综分析。
- **Metapredict 集成**：其调用 Metapredict 的方式可迁移到其他无序性分析流水线。
- **摘要 TSV 生成**（`bin/build_summary_tsv.py`）：可复用其聚合多分支指标的逻辑，用于自定义评估。
- **许可证**：仓库未明确说明许可证，需确认。

**注意**：以上可搬移点基于仓库提供的文件结构，具体实现细节需查看源码。

# genome_annotation_quality_nextflow_pipeline

Nextflow pipeline for large-scale protein structure prediction,
intrinsic disorder analysis, and genome annotation quality assessment
using **Protenix**, **Metapredict**, **PSAURON**, and **Interproscan**.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Overview

This repository contains a **Nextflow DSL2 pipeline** for:

- Large-scale protein structure prediction using Protenix
- Intrinsic disorder prediction using Metapredict
- Protein-coding sequence quality assessment using PSAURON
- Functional domain annotation and coverage profiling using InterProScan
- Automated chunking and HPC parallelisation
- Model processing and metric extraction
- Comparative plotting against reference proteome datasets
- One-row summary TSV per run, aggregating the headline plot metrics
  across all branches

The pipeline is designed for HPC environments (SLURM supported)
and supports GPU acceleration where appropriate.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Protenix-Mini Overview

Accurate protein structure prediction is often computationally intensive, limiting scalability for large-scale or real-world applications. Protenix-Mini is a lightweight, optimized variant of the Protenix framework designed to balance computational efficiency with high predictive accuracy. It achieves this through several key architectural refinements: replacing the multi-step AF3 diffusion sampler with a reduced-step Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE) sampler to lower inference overhead, pruning non-contributory Transformer components within the pairformer and diffusion modules, and incorporating an ESM-based protein language model to substitute the traditional MSA module—thereby eliminating costly MSA preprocessing. These modifications substantially reduce model complexity and runtime while maintaining high structural fidelity. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate only a minimal 1–5% decrease in performance relative to the full-scale model. Protenix-Mini therefore enables efficient, GPU-accelerated structure prediction suitable for large proteomes and resource-constrained environments, making it well suited for high-throughput genome annotation quality assessment workflows.
## Metapredict Overview

Intrinsically disordered proteins and intrinsically disordered regions (IDRs) play essential roles in cellular regulation, signaling, phase separation, and molecular recognition. Accurate identification of IDRs directly from sequence is therefore critical for understanding protein function at scale. Metapredict is a state-of-the-art disorder prediction tool designed for both high accuracy and extremely high throughput, enabling proteome-scale analyses in seconds. Developed with usability in mind, Metapredict is distributed as a web server, Python package, command-line interface, and Google Colab notebook. Leveraging deep learning–based predictions trained across diverse datasets, Metapredict V3 enables evolutionary-scale disorder analysis across thousands of proteomes. In this pipeline, Metapredict is integrated as a GPU-accelerated step to generate per-protein disorder metrics and comparative distributions against large multi-species reference datasets, facilitating genome-wide disorder profiling and annotation quality assessment.
## PSAURON Overview

Evaluating the accuracy of protein-coding sequences in genome annotations
is a challenging problem with no broadly applicable universal solution.

PSAURON (Protein Sequence Assessment Using a Reference ORF Network)
is a machine learning–based tool trained on a diverse dataset of over
1000 plant and animal genomes. It assigns a score to coding DNA or protein
sequences reflecting the likelihood that the sequence represents a genuine
protein-coding region.

PSAURON scores enable:

- Genome-wide protein annotation quality assessment
- Rapid identification of potentially spurious protein annotations
- Comparative overlay against large multi-species reference datasets

This pipeline integrates PSAURON scoring directly into structure and
disorder prediction workflows for multi-metric genome annotation QC.

## InterProScan Overview

Functional annotation of protein sequences is a cornerstone of genome
quality assessment. InterProScan integrates fifteen member databases —
including PFAM, PANTHER, GENE3D, SUPERFAMILY, FUNFAM, CDD, SMART, PRINTS,
HAMAP, PIRSF, PIRSR, SFLD, NCBIFAM, PROSITE_PROFILES and PROSITE_PATTERNS —
to assign protein family, domain, and functional site signatures, mapping
them where possible to the unified InterPro classification.

In this pipeline, InterProScan is used to compute two complementary
genome-quality metrics:

- **Per-library coverage**: the percentage of input proteins matched by
  each signature library, plus an overall "any IPR hit" total. This
  reveals which evidence sources are dominant for a given proteome and
  flags annotation gaps relative to reference organisms.
- **Per-protein domain coverage**: for every protein, the fraction of
  residues covered by the union of its IPR-bearing matches (overlapping
  hits merged so residues are not double-counted), giving a length-
  normalised score between 0 and 1. The distribution of this score
  across the proteome is a sensitive indicator of annotation quality —
  proteomes with many short, fragmented, or spurious annotations
  typically show a heavy excess of low-coverage proteins relative to
  well-annotated reference organisms.

The InterProScan branch is **off by default** and is enabled with
`--run_interpro true` (see [Choosing which branches run](#choosing-which-branches-run)).
Because InterProScan is computationally expensive, the pipeline
parallelises it by chunking the input FASTA, running each chunk
independently, and concatenating the per-chunk XML/TSV outputs before
plotting. The number of chunks matches however many chunks the Protenix
branch produced (set by `--chunk_size`); if Protenix is switched off,
it is the FASTA's sequence count divided by `--chunk_size`, rounded up.

Chunking uses greedy longest-processing-time-first (LPT) bin-packing
(`bin/balance_chunks.sh`): sequences are sorted by length descending and
each is assigned to whichever chunk currently has the smallest total
residue count. This keeps per-chunk runtime balanced even when large
multi-domain genes are clustered together in the input FASTA (naive
sequential N-sequences-per-chunk splitting can leave one chunk with
several giant outliers while others sit mostly idle). The assignment is
deterministic — the same input and chunk count always produce the same
chunks.



## Summary Metrics TSV

In addition to the per-branch plots and the combined PDF report, every
pipeline run emits a single-row TSV file
(`results/<dataset>_summary.tsv`) containing the headline numbers used
to construct the plots. This is intended for downstream tabular
aggregation — concatenating the summary TSVs across many runs gives a
single table comparing all queries on the same metrics.

The TSV always carries the same column schema. Columns for any branch
that was switched off are left blank rather than removed, so the layout
is stable across runs.

| Column                 | Source         | Description                                                                                       |
|------------------------|----------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `dataset`              | run parameter  | Dataset identifier (the FASTA basename)                                                           |
| `total_proteins`       | pLDDT PKL / FASTA | Number of proteins for which a mean pLDDT was computed; if Protenix is off, the number of sequences in the input FASTA |
| `prop_ge_70`           | Protenix       | Fraction of proteins with mean pLDDT ≥ 70 (y-axis of the GMM scatter plot)                        |
| `gmm_upper_prop`       | Protenix       | Weight of the upper component of a 2-component GMM fitted to the pLDDT distribution, with guided initialisation from the reference species (x-axis of the GMM scatter plot) |
| `disorder_prop_gt_0p5` | Metapredict    | Proportion of proteins with mean disorder score > 0.5                                             |
| `psauron_high_pct`     | PSAURON        | Percentage of proteins with `in-frame_score` ≥ 0.9 (the "High" bar of the PSAURON plot)           |
| `ipr_hit_pct`          | InterProScan   | Percentage of proteins with at least one IPR-bearing hit (the "any IPR hit" total from the InterPro coverage plot). Blank if `--run_interpro` is `false`. |

A single `BUILD_SUMMARY_TSV` process implements this stage. Because DSL2
does not cleanly support optional `path` inputs, `main.nf` passes a
placeholder file from `assets/` (`NO_FILE_PLDDT`, `NO_FILE_METAPREDICT`,
`NO_FILE_PSAURON`, `NO_FILE_IPR_XML`) for each branch that did not run,
and the process leaves the matching flag off the
`bin/build_summary_tsv.py` command line. The same mechanism lets
`PLOT_PLDDT` run without Metapredict; in that case it skips only the
disorder-coloured GMM scatter plot.


## Choosing which branches run

Each of the four analysis branches can be switched on or off
independently. At least one must be on; the pipeline stops with an error
if all four are off. The PDF report and summary TSV only include the
branches that ran.

| Parameter           | Default | Branch                                              |
|---------------------|---------|-----------------------------------------------------|
| `--run_protenix`    | `true`  | Protenix structure prediction and pLDDT plots       |
| `--run_metapredict` | `true`  | Metapredict disorder prediction and plots           |
| `--run_psauron`     | `true`  | PSAURON scoring and plots                           |
| `--run_interpro`    | `false` | InterProScan. `true` runs it; a path to an InterProScan XML file plots that XML instead |

Values are case-insensitive (`true`/`false`, `yes`/`no`, `1`/`0`).
For example, to skip the GPU-heavy Protenix step and run only the
sequence-based branches plus InterProScan:

```bash
nextflow run main.nf -profile singularity_slurm --fasta example.fasta --run_protenix false --run_interpro true --interpro_data /path/to/interpro_data
```



## Installation Instructions

Follow these steps to install and set up the **Nextflow Genome Annotation Quality Pipeline**:

### 1. Install Nextflow

Nextflow is required to run the pipeline.

```bash

curl -s https://get.nextflow.io | bash

mv nextflow ~/bin/

nextflow -version
```

> Ensure `~/bin` is in your `PATH` or adjust the path accordingly.

---

### 2. Install Java (if needed)

Nextflow requires Java 8+:

```bash

sudo apt-get install openjdk-11-jdk


java -version
```

---

### 3. Download the Pipeline Repository

```bash
git clone https://github.com/mesdaghi/genome_annotation_quality_nextflow_pipeline
cd genome_annotation_quality_nextflow_pipeline
```

---

### 4. Setup Singularity/ Apptainer Images

There are two options for setting up the Singularity/Apptainer images required for the pipeline:

#### 4.1 Use Pre-Built Images

The pre-built images are hosted on GitHub Container Registry and can be pulled directly using the download_containers.sh script:

First, make the script executable:
```bash
chmod +x bin/download_containers.sh
```

Make sure APPTAINER_TMP is set to a directory with sufficient space for the images, then run the script to download the images:
```bash
export APPTAINER_TMP=/path/to/temp_directory
mkdir -p APPTAINER_TMP
```

Then run the script to download the images:
```bash
bin/download_containers.sh /path/to/singularity_image_directory
```

#### 4.2 Build Images Locally

If you prefer to build the images locally or are a developer making modifications, you can build the images using a nox session. First, install pipx if you don't have it already:

```bash
python3 -m pip install --user pipx
python3 -m pipx ensurepath
```

Then install nox:

```bash
pipx install nox
```


Finally, build the singularity/apptainer images:

```bash
nox -s build_apptainer -- --output /path/to/singularity_images
```
### 5. Download InterProScan Data

The exact steps for downloading InterProScan data can be found here [InterProScan Data Download](https://interproscan-docs.readthedocs.io/en/v5/HowToUseViaContainer.html). But, in short, you can download the data using the following commands


```bash
curl -O http://ftp.ebi.ac.uk/pub/software/unix/iprscan/5/5.78-109.0/alt/interproscan-data-5.78-109.0.tar.gz

tar -pxzf interproscan-data-5.78-109.0.tar.gz
```

### 6. Run a Test Pipeline

Please specifiy the path to your singularity images directory in the singularity.config file before running the pipeline. (or as a parameter `--singularity_image_dir /path/to/singularity_images`)

There are two profiles available for testing:
1. 'singularity_local' — runs the pipeline locally using Singularity containers
2. 'singularity_slurm' — runs the pipeline on an HPC cluster with SLURM, using Singularity containers

```bash
nextflow run main.nf -profile slurm_local --fasta example.fasta --chunk_size 100 --singularity_image_dir /path/to/singularity_images

```
If using InterProScan, please specify the path to your InterProScan data directory in the singularity.config file before running the pipeline. (or as a parameter `--interpro_data /path/to/interpro_data`) For example:

```bash
nextflow run main.nf -profile slurm_local --fasta example.fasta --chunk_size 100 --singularity_image_dir /path/to/singularity_images --run_interpro true --interpro_data /path/to/interpro_data/interproscan-5.77-108.0/data/
```

- `--fasta` : Path to input FASTA file  
- `--chunk_size` : Number of sequences per Protenix chunk  
- `--singularity_image_dir` : Path to directory containing  
Singularity images (optional if set in config)
`--protenix_cahce `: Path to Protenix cache directory (optional, can also be set via nextflow.config)
`--run_protenix` : Run the Protenix branch (optional, default: true)
`--run_metapredict` : Run the Metapredict branch (optional, default: true)
`--run_psauron` : Run the PSAURON branch (optional, default: true)
`--run_interpro` : Enable InterPro branch. `true` = run InterProScan; `/path/to/x.xml` = plot only (optional, default: false)
`--interpro_data` : Path to InterProScan data directory (optional, can also be set via nextflow.config)

All output (plots, PKL files, CSVs) will be stored under `results/`.


---

### Notes

- Make sure your environments are accessible on the compute nodes.  
- Set `PROTENIX_CACHE` before running Protenix predictions.  


## Features

### Structure Prediction (Protenix)

- FASTA → Protenix JSON conversion
- JSON chunk splitting for parallel inference
- GPU-accelerated Protenix prediction
- Automatic model collection and aggregation
- pLDDT extraction into PKL datasets
- Distribution plotting vs reference organisms

### Disorder Prediction (Metapredict)

- GPU-accelerated disorder prediction
- Automatic overlay vs reference proteome disorder database
- Histogram and KDE density plots

### Protein-Coding Quality Assessment (PSAURON)

- GPU-accelerated PSAURON scoring
- Overlay of new dataset vs precomputed multi-species reference
- Histogram and KDE density plots
- Automated integration into Nextflow workflow

### Functional Domain Annotation (InterProScan)

- Optional, FASTA-driven InterProScan branch (`--run_interpro true`)
- Automatic chunking and parallel execution across HPC compute nodes
- Concatenation of per-chunk XML/TSV outputs into a single result
- Per-library coverage bar chart with the query highlighted alongside
  five reference model organisms
- Per-protein merged-domain coverage violin/box plot showing the
  distribution of residue-level IPR coverage across the proteome
- Tab-separated summary table of per-species coverage metrics
- Acceptance of a precomputed XML via `--run_interpro /path/to/xml`,
  skipping the (expensive) InterProScan step

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Workflow Diagram

                              FASTA
                /        |          |          \
               /         |          |           \
          PROTENIX  METAPREDICT  PSAURON  INTERPROSCAN (optional)
              |          |          |           |
           pLDDT PKL    CSV        CSV       XML / TSV
              |          |          |           |
          PLOT_PLDDT  PLOT_META  PLOT_PSAURON  PLOT_INTERPRO
              |          |          |           |
             PNG        PNG        PNG     PNG ×2 + TSV
                \        |          |           /
                 \       |          |          /
                            FINAL REPORT (PDF)
                                  +
                       BUILD_SUMMARY_TSV  →  <dataset>_summary.tsv
------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Requirements

### Core Software

- Nextflow ≥ 23
- Python 3.10
- CUDA-enabled GPU (recommended for Protenix, Metapredict, PSAURON)
- SLURM (optional, HPC environments)

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Running the Pipeline

### Basic Run

```bash
nextflow run main.nf -profile slurm --fasta after_461.fasta --chunk_size 100
```

### Parameters

| Parameter              | Description                                                                       |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| --chunk_size           | Number of sequences per Protenix chunk                                            |
| --ipr_chunks           | Number of length-balanced InterProScan chunks (default: 24)                       |
| --fasta                | Path to input FASTA file                                                          |
| --run_interpro         | Enable InterPro branch. `true` = run InterProScan; `/path/to/x.xml` = plot only   |
| --ipr_reference_json   | Path to reference model-organism JSON (default: `bin/ipr_coverage.json`)          |

### Running with the InterProScan branch

The InterProScan branch is opt-in. By default it is disabled.

```bash
# Full branch — runs InterProScan from scratch on the input FASTA
nextflow run main.nf -profile slurm \
    --fasta after_461.fasta \
    --run_interpro true

# Plot-only — skip the (expensive) InterProScan step and reuse a
# previously generated XML, paired with the dataset's FASTA
nextflow run main.nf -profile slurm \
    --fasta after_461.fasta \
    --run_interpro /path/to/precomputed_interproscan_output.xml

# Override the reference model-organism dataset
nextflow run main.nf -profile slurm \
    --fasta after_461.fasta \
    --run_interpro true \
    --ipr_reference_json /path/to/custom_ipr_coverage.json
```

Intermediate outputs:

## Example Output Images

### pLDDT Distribution Example


![pLDDT KDE Example](plddt_density_scipy_after_461.png)
## Proteome Structural Confidence Landscape

This plot positions each species according to two complementary measures of proteome structural quality derived from AlphaFold pLDDT scores, allowing the query proteome to be interpreted in the context of well-characterised reference organisms.

![Proteome Structural Confidence Landscape](plddt_gmm_scatter.png)

### Axes

**X-axis — GMM Upper Component Proportion**
Each species' pLDDT distribution is modelled as a two-component Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM), capturing the characteristic bimodal shape seen in most proteomes — a lower-confidence disordered peak and a higher-confidence structured peak. The x-axis shows the weight of the upper (higher pLDDT) component, i.e. the proportion of proteins belonging to the high-confidence structured peak. Species further right have a greater fraction of their proteome in the structured, high-confidence GMM component.

**Y-axis — Proportion ≥70 pLDDT**
A simpler, threshold-based measure of the same concept — the fraction of proteins with a mean pLDDT ≥ 70, a commonly used cutoff distinguishing confidently modelled from poorly modelled regions. The two axes are expected to correlate, but divergence between them can indicate unusual distributional shapes.

### Colour — Skew
Points are coloured by the skewness of each species' pLDDT distribution. Negative skew (purple) indicates a distribution pulled toward lower pLDDT values, typical of proteomes with a large disordered or low-complexity fraction. Positive skew (yellow) indicates a tail toward higher confidence values.

### Red circle — Query species
The input dataset is highlighted with a red circle and bold label, allowing its structural quality profile to be interpreted relative to reference proteomes. Its position gives an intuitive indication of whether the proteome resembles organisms with high structural coverage (top right, e.g. vertebrates) or those with more disordered or low-confidence proteomes (bottom left, e.g. parasitic protozoa).

### GMM initialisation
To ensure consistent and comparable fits across species, the GMM for each species is initialised using parameters averaged from six reference species — *Drosophila melanogaster*, *Homo sapiens*, *Rattus norvegicus*, *Mus musculus*, *Pan troglodytes*, and *Arabidopsis thaliana* — rather than random starting points.

### Metapredict Disorder Example

![Metapredict KDE Example](after_461_metapredict_mean_disorder_density_scipy.png)

### PSAURON Example

![PSAURON Example](psauron_categorical_distribution_new.png)

### InterPro Per-Library Coverage Example

This plot shows the percentage of input proteins matched by each
InterProScan signature library, with the query species highlighted on the
right. The final dark "Total (any IPR hit)" bar gives the headline
overall coverage figure (e.g. 58.4% for *Arabidopsis thaliana*).

![InterPro Per-Library Coverage Example](query_ipr_coverage.png)

#### How to interpret
- **Per-library bars** show what fraction of the proteome is matched by
  each library individually. A protein hit by both PFAM and PANTHER will
  contribute to both bars — these are not stacked, so summing across
  libraries does not give the total.
- **Total bar** shows the percentage of proteins with at least one hit
  from any IPR-bearing library — the canonical "InterPro coverage" figure.
- **Library order** is determined by aggregate hit count across all
  species in the reference set, so the most informative libraries
  appear leftmost.

### InterPro Per-Protein Coverage Distribution Example

This plot shows the distribution of length-normalised IPR coverage
across every protein in each proteome. For each protein, all IPR-bearing
hits are merged (overlapping intervals counted once) and the covered
residues divided by the protein length to give a score between 0 and 1.

![InterPro Per-Protein Coverage Distribution Example](query_ipr_longest_domain_coverage_distribution.png)

#### How to interpret
- **Violin shape** shows the density of coverage values at each level.
  Most well-annotated proteomes are bimodal: a peak at 0 (proteins with
  no IPR hit) and a peak near 1 (single-domain proteins fully covered
  by their domain).
- **Box overlay** shows the IQR and median (white line); the white
  diamond marks the mean.
- **Stats line** below the plot reports n, mean, median, and the count
  of zero-coverage proteins per species — the latter is often the most
  diagnostic single number for annotation quality.
- **Query species** appears at the right with a red border and is
  separated from the reference set by a dashed grey line.

------------------------------------------------------------------------
## Reference Datasets
### Protein Model Reference  
    bin/plddt_model_organisms.csv
### Disorder Reference

    bin/combined_proteome_disorder.pkl

### PSAURON Reference

    bin/combined_psauron_results.csv

Precomputed multi-species PSAURON score distribution used as background
for comparative overlay plots.

### InterPro Reference

    bin/ipr_coverage.json

Precomputed InterProScan coverage data for five reference model
organisms — *Arabidopsis thaliana*, *Drosophila melanogaster*,
*Homo sapiens*, *Mus musculus*, and *Saccharomyces cerevisiae* —
including per-library hit counts, overall coverage percentages, and
per-protein merged-domain coverage vectors. Used by `bin/plot_interpro.py`
to overlay the query proteome against well-characterised references.

To regenerate or extend this dataset, run the standalone reporter script

## 是什么

这是一个基于**整合结构建模（integrative structure modeling）**的脚本仓库，用于定位 Ecm29 蛋白在 26S 蛋白酶体上的结合位置。它利用 DSSO 化学交联数据（质谱鉴定）和已知的蛋白酶体结构（PDB: 5GJR），通过 IMP、MODELLER 和 PMI 工具构建 Ecm29 的构象模型，并确定其与蛋白酶体的相对位置。

## 亮点

- **整合多种数据源**：将化学交联（DSSO）、同源建模（MODELLER）、二级结构/无序区预测（PSIPRED）和冷冻电镜结构（5GJR）整合到一个建模流程中。
- **成熟的采样与统计分析**：使用 Gibbs 采样（Metropolis Monte Carlo）进行大规模构象搜索，并提供收敛性检验（Mann-Whitney U 检验、χ² 检验）和精度评估（RMSF）。
- **可并行化**：支持 SGE 集群提交脚本，可并行运行 500 个独立轨迹，适合高性能计算环境。
- **可测试性**：仓库包含测试脚本（`test/test.py`），并标记为“Testable: Yes”和“Parallelizeable: Yes”。

## 为何对本课题有用

该仓库直接涉及**固有无序区（IDR）** 的建模：Ecm29 的构象建模中明确使用了 PSIPRED 预测的**无序区**信息，并利用交联数据约束构象。对于 IDR/IDP 与分子互作（如 LLPS）的研究，此仓库提供了：
- **整合建模框架**：如何将实验约束（交联）与预测信息（无序区）结合，构建构象系综。
- **采样与收敛分析**：Gibbs 采样和统计检验方法可迁移到 IDP 构象系综的采样质量评估。
- **互作定位**：通过交联约束确定蛋白在复合物中的位置，类似方法可用于 IDP 与相分离伙伴的互作建模。

## 怎么用

- **主入口**：`production_scripts/smodeling.py` 是生产模拟脚本；`comparative_modeling/model_ecm29_352.py` 和 `model_ecm29_686.py` 用于构建 Ecm29 两个结构域的同源模型。
- **安装与依赖**：需要 [IMP](https://integrativemodeling.org)、[MODELLER](https://salilab.org/modeller) 和 [PMI](https://github.com/salilab/pmi)。依赖文件未在仓库中列出，但 README 提及这些工具。
- **输入数据**：`data` 目录包含 63 个 DSSO 交联（56 个分子内，7 个与 19S 蛋白酶体分子间）；模板序列和比对文件（`template.ali`, `aligs.pir`）；蛋白酶体结构来自 PDB 5GJR。
- **运行命令**：运行 `model_ecm29_352.py` 和 `model_ecm29_686.py` 生成同源模型，然后运行 `smodeling.py` 进行生产模拟。建议至少 500 个独立运行，每个运行 7500 个模型（共 3,750,000 个模型）。
- **分析脚本**：`analysis_scripts/` 包含收敛性检验（`MannWhitney.py`, `Precision_Pvalue_Calculation.py`）和精度评估（`RMSF_ECM29.py`）。
- **GPU 需求**：README 未说明是否需要 GPU，但 IMP 通常支持 CPU 并行，可能不需要 GPU。
- **调试示例**：`test/test.py` 提供测试，可用于断点调试。

## 核心 idea

核心方法学是**整合结构建模**：将多种实验约束（如化学交联）和生物信息学预测（如无序区）统一转化为空间约束，通过蒙特卡洛采样生成构象系综，并用统计检验评估采样收敛性。其创新点在于如何将稀疏的交联数据转化为有效的距离约束，从而在低分辨率下定位蛋白互作界面。

## 可搬移点

- **交联约束处理逻辑**：`production_scripts/smodeling.py` 中如何将 DSSO 交联转化为距离约束的代码，可解耦后用于其他 IDP 互作建模。
- **收敛性检验脚本**：`analysis_scripts/MannWhitney.py` 和 `Precision_Pvalue_Calculation.py` 可独立使用，用于评估任何构象系综的采样质量。
- **RMSF 计算**：`analysis_scripts/RMSF_ECM29.py` 可迁移到 IDP 构象系综的柔性分析。
- **同源建模脚本**：`comparative_modeling/model_ecm29_*.py` 展示了如何结合模板和预测信息构建模型，可借鉴到 IDP 结构域建模。
- **License**：CC BY-SA 4.0，允许修改和再分发，但需注明出处并保持相同许可。

（注：部分脚本如 `util/` 下的工具未详细说明，但可能包含辅助功能。）

# Localizing ecm29 on the proteasome using integrative structure modeling

These scripts demonstrate the use of [IMP](https://integrativemodeling.org), [MODELLER](https://salilab.org/modeller), and [PMI](https://github.com/salilab/pmi) in the modeling of the proteasome/ecm29 complex using DSSO chemical cross-links.

## Comparative modeling of ecm29 (2 domains)
Representation of ecm29 relied on (i) comparative models of 2 ecm29 domains built with MODELLER 9.17 (Sali and Blundell, 1993) based on the known related structures detected by HHPred (Soding, 2005; Soding et al. 2005) and (ii) secondary structure and disordered regions predicted by PSIPRED based on the ecm29 sequence (Buchan et al., 2013; Jones, 1999); see file `ecm29.hhp` in the `comparative_modeling` directory.

The sequences of the two templates (1U6G and 3W3W) and ecm29 can be found in `template.ali`.
The two templates have PDB code 1U6G and 3W3W respectively, with alignment to ecm29 in `aligs.pir`.
To obtain the comparative models, run `model_ecm29_352.py` and
`model_ecm29_686.py`.

## Input data (directory `data`):

63 DSSO cross-links involving ecm29 were identified via mass spectrometry; 56 of these cross-links were intramolecular and seven were intermolecular with the 19S proteasome, informing respectively the ecm29 conformation and the localization of ecm29 relative to the proteasome.

The 26S proteasome structure used was obtained from the PDB (code 5GJR); it was determined primarily based on a cryo-EM density map at 3.8Å resolution (EMDB code: 9508) {Huang, 2016 NSMB}.

## Running the simulations (directory `production_scripts`):

  - `smodeling.py`: PMI modeling scripts for running the production simulations:
    The search for good-scoring models relied on Gibbs sampling, based on the
    Metropolis Monte Carlo algorithm. We suggest producing at least 3,750,000
    models from 500 independent runs, each starting from a different initial
    conformation of ecm29 to have proper statistics.

  - `job_26s.sub`: SGE cluster based submission script to run automatically
    500 independent runs.

  - The compressed 500 independent trajectories are accessible at:
    `/salilab/park1/ilan/ECM29/ECM29_19S/modeling[0-499].tar`

## Analyzing the simulations (directory `analysis_scripts`):

Various scripts to analysis the simulations. we give more details scripts that allows us to test for sampling convergence.

  - `Select_Top_Scoring_models.sh`: basic bash scripts that read and summarize
    information found in the stat file generated by PMI.

  - `Random_Subset.sh`: we test if adding more models improves our sampling
    of top scores. The input to the script is a list of all the `Total_Score`
    from the simulations. For each subset, we perform 100 sub-samplings to
    compute error bars. We give the file twice to check how the error bars
    vary.

  - `MannWhitney.py`: we test if the distribution from two independent
    subsets are not unsimilar.

  - The good-scoring models that have been selected for precision-based
    clustering based on RMSD metric are located in:
    `/salilab/park1/ilan/ECM29/ECM29_19S/Clustered_Models.tar.gz`
    The file name format is `${trajectory_number}_${frame_number}.rmf3`

  - `Precision_Pvalue_Calculation.py`: Given an RMSD matrix, we compute the
    𝛘2-test for homogeneity of proportions{McDonald, 2014} and compute the
    best precision for which sampling has converged.

  - `RMSF_ECM29.py`: Given a list of structures, compute the average RMSF,
    which indicates the precision of the structures in a cluster.

## Plotting the results (directory `plotting_scripts`)

GNUPlot scripts for generating figures from the paper.
